Big companies recruit final-year students in the autumn (秋招) and again in the spring (春招), and an 应届毕业生, someone graduating this year, has a special status: many posts are open only to them. A Chinese CV (简历) is usually a single page and often includes a photo, date of birth and home town, which a British CV would leave out. Job adverts list 岗位职责 (duties) and 任职要求 (requirements), and 五险一金, five kinds of social insurance plus a housing fund, is a standard part of the package.

dabu1-u2-1i.title: 一方面 … 另一方面 … — on the one hand, on the other
dabu1-u2-1i.body: Use it to set out two sides of something: two reasons, or a good point and a bad one. The second half often takes 也 or 又. It's more structured than just listing, and it's at home in discussions and essays. Don't confuse it with 一边…一边…, which is two actions at the same time. 那几年我一方面学到了很多东西，另一方面身体真的吃不消。 (In those years I learned a lot, but my health couldn't take it.)

dabu1-u2-4l.title: 不仅 … 还 / 也 / 而且 … — not only … but also
dabu1-u2-4l.body: 不仅 is the written cousin of 不但 (进步 3). The second half takes 还, 也 or 而且. When the two halves have different subjects, 不仅 goes before the first subject: 不仅小雨在加班，陈明也…. 多吃点儿苦，不仅能学到更多东西，还能更快地升职加薪。 (Putting up with hardship not only teaches you more, but gets you promoted faster.)

dabu1-u2-2j.title: 难免 — bound to happen
dabu1-u2-2j.body: 难免 says something is hard to avoid, and so understandable. It often takes 会. It's a kind way to excuse a mistake, your own or someone else's. It can also stand alone at the end: 加班难免. 我们这一行，加班难免。 (In our line of work, some overtime's unavoidable.)

dabu1-u2-5i.title: 则 and 甚至 — writing a balanced argument
dabu1-u2-5i.body: A balanced piece gives both sides before its own view. 则 is a written 'whereas, on the other hand'. It goes after the second subject, never before it. In speech you'd use 可是 instead. 甚至 'even' pushes a point one step further. 支持的人认为年轻人应该多吃点儿苦，反对的人则认为健康更重要。 (Supporters say the young should put up with hardship; opponents say health matters more.)

dabu1-u2-2i.title: Culture · 996, and the words around it
dabu1-u2-2i.body: The number 996 became a household word in China in 2019, when programmers started an online campaign against companies that expected staff to work from 9 am to 9 pm, six days a week. Some business leaders defended long hours as the price of success; many more people criticised them, and the debate has never really stopped. Under China's labour law, a schedule like that goes well beyond the limits on working hours and overtime, and the authorities have said more than once that overtime must follow the law. Many companies have publicly dropped such schedules, though long hours remain common in some industries.

dabu1-u3-1l.title: 按照 or 根据? — according to
dabu1-u3-1l.body: Both translate as 'according to'. 按照 means following something: a rule, a request, a plan. 根据 means basing something on evidence: a survey, figures, the situation. With 要求 and 规定, choose 按照; with 调查, 结果 and 情况, choose 根据. In speech, 按 alone is common too: 按他们说的改. 我们可以按照他们的要求调一下颜色。 (We can tweak the colour the way they asked.)

dabu1-u3-1l.title: 请查收, 如有问题 — formal email phrases
dabu1-u3-1l.body: A formal Chinese email is built from set phrases, and using them is expected, not stiff. Open with 尊敬的 + surname + title and a colon, then 您好！ on its own line. At the end, 此致 goes on a line of its own and 敬礼！ on the next, followed by your name and the date. 修改后的方案请见附件，请查收。 (Please find the revised design attached.)

dabu1-u3-1l.title: WeChat or email? — one message, two registers
dabu1-u3-1l.body: The same message changes a lot between a chat and an email. WeChat drops subjects and uses 你, 了 and 吧. Email uses 您, full sentences and written words: 已 for 已经, 如 for 要是, 与 for 跟, 将 for 会. 方案发你了，你看一下。→ 方案已发送，请查收。 (Sent you the design, have a look. → The design has been sent. Please check your inbox.)

dabu1-u3-4j.title: 于 and 将 — two words that make it formal
dabu1-u3-4j.body: 于 is a written 在 before times and places, and it's built into words like 位于 and 关于. 将 is a written 会 or 要 for the future, and also a written 把. Both belong in emails, reports and notices. In a WeChat message they sound like a press release. 感谢您于5月11日提出的宝贵意见。 (Thank you for your valuable comments of 11 May.)

dabu1-u3-2g.title: Culture · Meetings, WeChat and email
dabu1-u3-2g.body: In most Chinese offices, day-to-day work happens on WeChat, in 工作群 (work group chats) that often include the client. Messages are short, fast and friendly, full of 好的 and 收到 ('got it'), and people are expected to reply quickly, often even after hours. Email is kept for things that need a record: proposals, contracts, quotes and meeting minutes (会议纪要). A common habit is to send the email and then post a quick WeChat message to say so: 邮件已发，请查收.

dabu1-u4-1i.title: 与其 … 不如 … — rather than
dabu1-u4-1i.body: 'Rather than A, better to B.' The speaker has weighed up both and rejects A. It's for advice and decisions, and works in speech and writing alike. Both halves are usually verb phrases. 与其为了钱把自己累坏，不如先把上海店做好。 (Rather than wearing yourself out for the money, why not get the Shanghai restaurant right first?)

dabu1-u4-1j.title: 宁可 … 也 … — I'd rather
dabu1-u4-1j.body: The thing after 宁可 is a cost you're willing to pay: 'I'd rather A, so as to B' (也要), or 'I'd rather A than B' (也不). That's the difference from 与其…不如…, where A is the option you turn down. 宁愿 means the same as 宁可. 我宁可少挣一点儿，也要把一件事做好。 (I'd rather earn a bit less and do one thing properly.)

dabu1-u4-2j.title: 成语 — four-character idioms
dabu1-u4-2j.body: 成语 are set phrases, most of them four characters long, and many come from old stories. Each works like one word. 半途而废 is a verb phrase: 'give up halfway'. 三心二意 and 一心一意 describe how someone does something, and can take 地 before a verb. 一举两得 usually comes after 就是, 真是 or 那就…了. One or two in a paragraph adds polish; more sounds showy. 现在把它放在一边，半途而废，多可惜。 (Putting it to one side now would mean giving up halfway. What a shame.)

dabu1-u4-4g.title: 趁 and 至于 — while you can; as for
dabu1-u4-4g.body: 趁 means 'while the chance is there': 趁年轻 while you're young, 趁热吃 eat it while it's hot. 至于 turns to a related topic, 'as for', often to give your own case last. 趁年轻，多挣点儿钱。 (Earn as much as you can while you're young.)

dabu1-u4-2i.title: Culture · Idioms, and the spring job-hop
dabu1-u4-2i.body: 成语 are fixed expressions, usually of four characters, and there are thousands of them. Many sum up an old story. 半途而废 comes from a tale about a woman who cut through the cloth on her loom to show her husband what it meant to give up his studies halfway. Others are simply vivid: 三心二意 is 'three hearts and two minds'. Educated speakers use them in speeches, essays and everyday chat, so a few, learned with how they're used, go a long way.

dabu2-u1-3k.title: 倒是 … 就是 … — fine, it's just that
dabu2-u1-3k.body: A very spoken way to weigh something up: grant one point with 倒是, then give the real problem with 就是 (or 不过, 可是). It sounds fair and a little tentative, which makes it good for turning something down gently. You can also flip it: 我倒是不怕没有电梯 'I don't mind about the lift', with the worry coming next. 房间倒是挺大的，就是离地铁站太远了。 (The room's big enough, it's just too far from the metro.)

dabu2-u1-3i.title: 算下来 and 不到哪里去 — adding up, playing down
dabu2-u1-3i.body: 算下来 means 'when you add it all up', and is the natural way to give a total or a conclusion after some sums. The pattern verb + 下来 also works with time: 一年下来 'over a whole year'. Adjective + 不到哪里去 plays something down: 'it won't be all that ….' It's reassuring and very spoken. 押一付三，再加上中介费，这样算下来，一开始就得交两万七。 (One down, three up front, plus the agent's fee: all told, that's twenty-seven thousand to start with.)

dabu2-u1-5i.title: 由 … 承担, 须, 不得 — the language of contracts
dabu2-u1-5i.body: Contracts use a register of their own. 由 says who does or pays something: 由乙方承担 'borne by Party B'. 须 is a written 必须 'must', 应 a written 应该 'shall', and 不得 a written 不能 or 不可以 'may not'. Dates run 自…起至…止 'from … to …'. In a lease, 甲方 is the landlord and 乙方 the tenant. 水电费由乙方承担。 (Water and electricity are paid by the tenant.)

dabu2-u1-2h.title: Spoken → written: the same deal, two ways
dabu2-u1-2h.body: What 陈妈妈 says on the stairs and what her contract says are the same deal in two registers. Swap 你 and 我 for 甲方 and 乙方, 得 and 要 for 须 and 应, 大概 for 约, 就是 'that is' for 即, and 从…到… for 自…起至…止. Don't bring these into conversation: 乙方须付清租金 at the dinner table would get a laugh. 房间大概十六平米。→ 面积约十六平方米。 (The room's about sixteen square metres.)

dabu2-u1-2i.title: Culture · Renting in Shanghai
dabu2-u1-2i.body: Most young people in Shanghai rent, and many share. 整租 means renting a whole flat; 合租 means taking a room in a shared one, with a shared kitchen and bathroom and a flatmate you may not choose. The standard terms are 押一付三: a month's rent as deposit, plus three months paid in advance, so moving in costs four months' rent at once. Agents (中介) usually charge a fee too, often around a month's rent, which is why a room found through a friend or a colleague's neighbour is such a prize. Bills are 水电煤, water, electricity and gas, and rent is almost always paid by phone.

dabu2-u2-4g.title: 必须 and 不必 — must and needn't
dabu2-u2-4g.body: 必须 'must' is strong and a little formal; in speech people often say 得 děi instead. Its negative is not 不必须 but 不必 or 不用, 'needn't'. For 'mustn't', use 不能, 不许 or, in writing, 不得. 必须 can also stand as the predicate: 这是必须的 'that's a must'. 吃剩的饭菜和用过的纸巾必须分开扔。 (Leftover food and used tissues must go in separately.)

dabu2-u2-1h.title: 否则 — otherwise
dabu2-u2-1h.body: 否则 means 'otherwise, if not': A is what should happen, B the consequence if it doesn't. It starts the second clause, often with 就 or 会 after it. It's a little formal; in speech 不然 or 要不然 is more common, and 陈妈妈 uses both. 必须分开扔，否则我这个志愿者不是白当了？ (It has to go in separately, otherwise what am I volunteering for?)

dabu2-u2-3j.title: 由于 — because of (in writing)
dabu2-u2-3j.body: 由于 is a more formal 因为. It usually comes in the first clause, and pairs well with 因此 'therefore'. Unlike 因为, it doesn't normally come after the result: say 由于下雨，比赛取消了, not 比赛取消了，由于下雨. It can also go straight before a noun: 由于时间关系 'for reasons of time'. 以前由于不分类，大部分垃圾只能埋掉、烧掉。 (Before, because nothing was sorted, most rubbish could only be buried or burned.)

dabu2-u2-7i.title: 以便 — so that (in writing)
dabu2-u2-7i.body: 以便 introduces the purpose of the first clause: 'so that, in order to'. It always comes at the start of the second clause, never the first. It belongs in notices, reports and articles; in speech, say 好 or 这样 instead: 带个杯子，这样就不用一次性的了. 出门带上自己的杯子，以便少用一次性用品。 (Take your own cup when you go out, so that you use fewer disposable things.)

dabu2-u2-2i.title: Culture · Shanghai sorts its rubbish
dabu2-u2-2i.body: On 1 July 2019 Shanghai's regulations on household waste took effect, and the city became one of the first in China to make sorting compulsory. Households must separate four kinds of rubbish, each with its own colour of bin: 可回收物 (recyclables, blue), 有害垃圾 (hazardous waste such as rechargeable batteries, old medicine and fluorescent tubes, red), 湿垃圾 (wet rubbish, food waste, brown) and 干垃圾 (dry rubbish, everything else, black). The national standard, used in other cities, calls the last two 厨余垃圾 and 其他垃圾. Residents who don't sort can be fined.

dabu2-u3-2k.title: 随着 — as, along with
dabu2-u3-2k.body: 随着 links two changes: as one thing develops, another follows. The part after 随着 is a noun phrase, often ending in 的发展, 的变化 or 的增加, and the second clause usually has 越来越, 也 or 开始. It's common in writing and in thoughtful speech. 随着城市化的发展，越来越多的人离开乡村。 (As urbanisation goes on, more and more people are leaving the countryside.)

dabu2-u3-5l.title: 不是 … 而是 … — not A, but B
dabu2-u3-5l.body: Use it to correct a mistaken idea and put the right one in its place. It's stronger and neater than 不是A，是B, and more at home in writing and discussion. Both halves should be the same kind of thing: two nouns, two verbs or two clauses. 问题不是东西不好，而是没有人帮他们把故事讲好。 (The problem isn't that the baskets aren't good; it's that nobody's helping them tell their story.)

dabu2-u3-5i.title: 一 … 就是 … — once you start, it's a lot
dabu2-u3-5i.body: This pattern stresses that an amount is large, or a time long: once the action starts, it goes on for that long. 一走就是四十多年 'left, and was gone for more than forty years'. The amount after 就是 is the point of the sentence, so say it with some weight. 我十九岁那年去北京打工，一走就是四十多年。 (At nineteen I went to Beijing to find work, and I've been away for more than forty years.)

dabu2-u3-3h.title: 变, 变成, 变得 and -化 — talking about change
dabu2-u3-3h.body: 变 goes straight before a short adjective: 变小, 变老. 变成 is 'turn into' and takes a noun: 变成一个篮子. 变得 takes a fuller description: 变得更安静. The suffix 化, which you met in 进步 5, turns a word into a process: 城市化 'urbanisation', 现代化 'modernisation'. 城市在长大，乡村却在变老。 (The cities are growing up, but the villages are growing old.)

dabu2-u3-2i.title: Culture · Leaving home, going home
dabu2-u3-2i.body: In 1980 about one in five people in China lived in towns and cities; today it's about two in three. Much of that change was made by migrant workers (农民工), nearly three hundred million of them, who left villages to work in factories, on building sites and in restaurants. Under the household registration system (户口), many could not easily bring their children to the city's schools, so millions of children grew up with grandparents at home: the 留守儿童, 'left-behind children'. Their parents' wages paid for houses, school fees and university, and the cost was measured in years apart.

dabu2-u4-2h.title: 仿佛 — as if
dabu2-u4-2h.body: 仿佛 is a literary 好像: 'as if, it seemed'. It goes before the verb or the whole clause, and can close with 一样 or 似的. Use it for impressions and comparisons in descriptive writing. In conversation, 好像 or 像…一样 sounds more natural, but Mark uses 仿佛 once, carefully, and it works. 走在梧桐树下面，我仿佛回到了伦敦。 (Walking under the plane trees, it's as if I'm back in London.)

dabu2-u4-2h.title: Doubled words — making a description come alive
dabu2-u4-2h.body: Doubling makes a description warmer and more vivid. A doubled adjective takes 的 (高高的, 软软的) or 地 before a verb (慢慢地). Some adjectives come in fixed ABB forms: 热乎乎 'nice and hot'. And 一片一片 or 一条条 means 'one by one' or 'row upon row'. Don't double adjectives that already have 很 or 非常 in front of them. 路两边的梧桐树高高的。 (The plane trees along the roads stand tall.)

dabu2-u4-5h.title: 不禁 and 忍不住 — can't help it
dabu2-u4-5h.body: 不禁 means a reaction happened by itself: you found yourself laughing, stopping or remembering. It's written and a little literary, and goes before the verb. 忍不住 means the same and is used in speech too; it can also mean you tried not to and failed, and it can take a negative after it (忍不住不看). 我不禁停下来看了半天。 (I couldn't help stopping to stare.)

dabu2-u4-1i.title: 既 … 又 … — both at once
dabu2-u4-1i.body: You met 既…又… in 大步 1. It joins two qualities, or two roles, of one person or thing, and it's tidier and more written than 又…又…. It's good for showing that something is two things at once: 既像一个租客，又像一个儿子. 又…又… is commoner in speech, especially with short adjectives: 又闷又热. 在她面前，我既像一个租客，又像一个儿子。 (With her, I'm part tenant, part son.)

dabu2-u4-2i.title: Culture · A little Shanghainese
dabu2-u4-2i.body: Shanghainese (上海话) belongs to the Wu family of Chinese, and a Mandarin speaker who hasn't learned it can understand very little. You don't need it to live in Shanghai: everyone speaks Mandarin, and many younger people now speak Shanghainese less than their grandparents do. But a few words will make an auntie smile. 侬好 (roughly 'nong ho') is 'hello', 阿拉 ('ah-lah') is 'we' or 'I', 侬 ('nong') is 'you', and 谢谢侬 ('shia-shia nong') is 'thank you'. 侬晓得伐？ is 'Did you know?', with 伐 as the question particle, like 吗. 嗲 ('dia') means lovely or charming, and has made its way into Mandarin.

dabu3-u1-3i.title: …的同时: while, at the same time as
dabu3-u1-3i.body: 的同时 joins two things that come together, very often a benefit and its cost: 'while A, B too'. A is a verb phrase or clause before 的同时, and the second half usually has 也 or 还. With 在 in front it sounds more written. It's the natural way to be fair in an argument: grant the good side, then add the other. 方便的同时，也要留个心眼。 (Enjoy the convenience, but keep your wits about you.)

dabu3-u1-2g.title: 靠, 全靠 and 离不开: depending on something
dabu3-u1-2g.body: 靠 means 'rely on, depend on', and can go straight before a second verb to say how something is done: 靠直播卖竹篮 'sell baskets by livestream'. 全靠 is 'depend entirely on'. 离不开 'can't do without' is the everyday way to say how much you need something. 依赖 is the formal word, common in articles and often a little critical. 再…也… 'however …, still …' often comes with them. 手机再方便，也不能全靠它。 (However handy your phone is, you can't rely on it for everything.)

dabu3-u1-2g.title: Culture · Paying by phone
dabu3-u1-2g.body: Since the mid-2010s China has become one of the most cashless places on earth. Almost every shop and market stall shows a payment QR code (收款码), and customers scan it with WeChat Pay or Alipay and type in the amount; in bigger shops the till scans a code on the customer's phone instead. Metro gates, bills, hospital fees and red envelopes all work the same way, and friends split the bill by transferring money in a chat.

dabu3-u1-3h.title: 不见得 and 未必: not necessarily
dabu3-u1-3h.body: Both soften a claim to 'not necessarily'. 不见得 is spoken and a little sceptical; 未必 is more written. Use them to push back gently on a generalisation without claiming the opposite: 年纪大不见得就学不会 doesn't say old people learn easily, only that age isn't the whole story. They often take 就 after them. 老人需要的，不见得是更先进的技术。 (What older people need isn't necessarily more advanced technology.)

dabu3-u1-1i.title: 扫, 刷, 转, 付: paying in Shanghai
dabu3-u1-1i.body: Shanghai pays by phone, and the verbs are short. 扫 is 'scan': 我扫你 means 'I'll scan your code'. 刷 is 'swipe', for bank cards, travel cards and even your face. 转 is 'transfer': 我转给你. In speech you 付钱; on a sign, a bill or in an article you 支付 or 付款, and send money by 转账. 我扫你还是你扫我？ (Shall I scan you, or will you scan me?)

dabu3-u2-2h.title: 即使 … 也 …: even if
dabu3-u2-2h.body: 即使 introduces a condition, real or imagined, and 也 says the result holds anyway: 'even if'. It's a touch more formal than 就算…也…, and different from 虽然…但是…, which is about facts. 即使 can come before or after the subject, but 也 always goes after the subject of the second clause. 即使…再… 'however much' is common too. 即使没有算法，我也会刷。 (Even without the algorithm, I'd still scroll.)

dabu3-u2-2h.title: Culture · Short video and 'traffic'
dabu3-u2-2h.body: China's short-video apps, led by Douyin (the Chinese sister of TikTok) and Kuaishou, have more than a billion users between them, and the average user spends over two hours a day watching. Feeds are driven by recommendation algorithms (算法) that learn from every swipe, which is why one cooking video can fill your screen with cooking.

dabu3-u2-3g.title: 所谓: what's known as, so-called
dabu3-u2-3g.body: 所谓 introduces a term and explains it: 所谓X，就是Y 'X means Y'. 这就是所谓的X 'this is what's called X' names something you've just described. New terms usually go in quotation marks. Said with a raised eyebrow, 所谓的 can sound sceptical, like English 'so-called'. 这就是所谓的“碎片化”。 (That's what they call 'fragmentation'.)

dabu3-u2-1f.title: 不在于 … 而在于 …: where the point really lies
dabu3-u2-1f.body: 在于 'lies in, rests on' is written and thoughtful. 关键在于 'the key lies in' names what matters most. 不在于A，而在于B corrects a wrong idea of where a problem lies. It's a more formal cousin of 不是…而是… from 大步 2, and good for the turn in an argument. 问题不在于短视频，而在于我们还能不能控制自己。 (The problem doesn't lie in short video, but in whether we can still control ourselves.)

dabu3-u2-5i.title: 何况: besides, let alone
dabu3-u2-5i.body: 何况 adds a further, often stronger reason: 'besides, what's more'. After 连…都… or a negative, (更)何况 means 'let alone', often as a rhetorical question. It's a little bookish, and very useful in writing and careful argument. 何况，短视频本身并不是坏东西。 (Besides, short video isn't a bad thing in itself.)

dabu3-u3-4f.title: 我不同意 and 这一点我同意: agreeing and disagreeing
dabu3-u3-4f.body: In a discussion, disagree with the idea, not the person: 我不同意这种说法 or 我不同意这种看法 sounds far better than a flat 你错了. 这一点我同意 grants one point before you add your own. 我不完全同意 is softer still. 同意 takes a person, an idea or a clause directly: say 我同意你, never 我同意跟你. 我不同意“AI会取代设计师”这种说法。 (I don't agree that AI will replace designers.)

dabu3-u3-2f.title: 话虽如此: that may be so, but
dabu3-u3-2f.body: 话虽如此 'though that is so' accepts what has just been said, then pushes back. It's more formal than 话是这么说 from 大步 1, and works in discussion, essays and speeches alike. The second half often has 但是, 也 or 还是. 话虽如此，这次不一样。 (That may be so, but this time it's different.)

dabu3-u3-2g.title: 反过来说: looked at the other way round
dabu3-u3-2g.body: 反过来说 turns an argument round: 'conversely, on the other hand'. Use it to show that the same fact has another side, or to state the reverse of what's just been said. It isn't a flat contradiction, so it keeps a debate friendly. 反过来说，如果基础工作交给AI，新人就能把时间花在更重要的地方。 (Look at it the other way round: if the groundwork goes to AI, new people can spend their time on more important things.)

dabu3-u3-2h.title: 归根结底: when all's said and done
dabu3-u3-2h.body: 归根结底 'going back to the root' sums up an argument: 'in the final analysis, at the end of the day'. It opens the closing sentence, or goes before the verb. Save it for your conclusion: used every other line, it sounds pompous. 客户要的归根结底不是一百张图，而是一个对的想法。 (At the end of the day, what the client wants isn't a hundred images but one right idea.)

dabu3-u3-2h.title: Culture · AI and the people who make things
dabu3-u3-2h.body: Generative AI (生成式人工智能) arrived in a rush in China after 2022. Chinese tech companies launched dozens of large models, and design, advertising and online-shopping firms were among the first to use AI images for product photos, posters and first drafts. Freelance illustrators and junior designers felt the change first, and 'AI will replace you' became a joke and a worry at the same time.

dabu3-u3-1g.title: 与其 … 不如 … again, with 取代 and 代替
dabu3-u3-1g.body: You met 与其…不如… in 大步 1. In an argument or a speech it's a strong way to recommend: reject one course, propose another. 取代 is 'replace, take the place of', usually for good and on a big scale: jobs, technologies. 代替 is lighter and can be temporary, and can take a verb after it: 马克代替她开会 'Mark went to the meeting in her place'. 与其担心被取代，不如想清楚哪些事只有人能做。 (Rather than worrying about being replaced, be clear about what only people can do.)

dabu3-u4-1i.title: 据报道, 据悉, 据了解: giving a source
dabu3-u4-1i.body: News gives its sources with 据 'according to'. 据报道 is 'it is reported', 据悉 'it is understood' (the source isn't named), 据了解 'we understand', and 据…介绍 'according to …'. They open the sentence and are followed by a comma. In speech you'd say 听说 or 新闻上说 instead. 据报道，最近网上流传“商家可以不收现金”的说法。 (According to reports, a claim that 'shops can refuse cash' has been going round online.)

dabu3-u4-2h.title: 表示 and 称: what people said
dabu3-u4-2h.body: Reports rarely use 说. 表示 'stated' is neutral and formal: it's what officials, managers and experts do. 称 'said, claimed' is shorter, common after a name and in headlines, and can suggest the paper is only passing the claim on. 介绍 'explained' is for background. A comma or a colon comes after them. 有关部门表示，这是谣言。 (The authorities stated that it was a rumour.)

dabu3-u4-2h.title: Headlines: reading them like a telegram
dabu3-u4-2h.body: Headlines are short and dense. They drop 了, 的 and most measure words, prefer one-character written verbs like 获 'win' and 将 'will', and often set two phrases side by side, with a space or a colon between. Read the headline as a telegram, then find the full sentence in the first paragraph. 竹编年货走俏　山村直播一月卖出八千件 → 竹编年货卖得很好，一个山村一个月在直播中卖出了八千件。 (Bamboo New Year goods sell well: a village sells eight thousand in a month by livestream.)

dabu3-u4-3h.title: 截至, 余, 近 and 超过: numbers in the news
dabu3-u4-3h.body: 截至 'as of, up to' gives the date a figure is counted to. Don't confuse it with 截止 'to close', as in 截止日期 'deadline'. 余 is a written 多 'more than' and comes straight after the number: 八千余件. 近 means 'nearly': 近一个月. 超过 is 'more than, over'. 截至1月20日，合作社共卖出竹编产品八千余件。 (As of 20 January, the co-operative had sold more than 8,000 bamboo items.)

dabu3-u4-2i.title: Culture · Reading the news, and the family group chat
dabu3-u4-2i.body: Chinese news has a register of its own. A report opens with a dense first paragraph that answers who, what, when and how many, and a newspaper marks its own reporting with 本报讯, 'this paper reports'. Sources come with 据: 据报道, 据悉, 据了解. Officials 表示; people making a claim 称. Headlines often come in two parts and drop the small grammatical words.

dabu4-u1-2i.title: 说到底: when it comes down to it
dabu4-u1-2i.body: 说到底 'if you talk it through to the bottom' strips a question down to its real cause or core. It's the spoken cousin of 归根结底 from 大步 3, warmer and less formal, and it often opens the sentence that says what someone really feels. Use it once, at the point where you get to the heart of things. 说到底，还是怕。 (When it comes down to it, it's fear.)

dabu4-u1-2i.title: 何必 and 难道: making a point with a question
dabu4-u1-2i.body: Both turn a question into an argument. 何必 'why must, what's the point of' says something is unnecessary: 何必呢？ on its own means 'why bother?'. 难道 'surely you don't mean' challenges an assumption and expects the answer no; the sentence usually ends with 吗. Both can sound sharp, so soften them with a smile, or with 其实 before your next point. 为了结婚而结婚，何必呢？ (Why marry just for the sake of it?)

dabu4-u1-2i.title: 为了 … 而 …: for the sake of
dabu4-u1-2i.body: In 为了A而B, A is the purpose and B the action taken for it; 而 links them. It's more written than plain 为了…, and it's the natural way to criticise an action done for the wrong reason: 为了结婚而结婚 'marrying for the sake of marrying'. 因为A而B works the same way for causes. 不能为了完成任务而随便找个人。 (You can't just pick anyone for the sake of getting it done.)

dabu4-u1-2i.title: Culture · Pressure to marry, and a contested label
dabu4-u1-2i.body: 催婚, 'hurrying someone to marry', peaks at Spring Festival and other holidays, when young people go home and parents, aunts and uncles ask the same question: 有对象了吗? 'Are you seeing anyone?' For many parents, marriage is simply the next stage of life, and behind the nagging is a real fear: who will look after their child when they are gone?

dabu4-u1-2k.title: 毕竟 and 话说回来: being fair to the other side
dabu4-u1-2k.body: 毕竟 'after all' gives the fact that explains or excuses something, and it goes before the verb or at the start of the clause. 话说回来 'that said, mind you' turns the conversation back to the other side of the argument. Together they let you disagree with someone without being unfair to them. 毕竟是两代人，想法不一样很正常。 (You're two generations, after all; it's normal to think differently.)

dabu4-u2-1l.title: 不得不 and 只好: no choice
dabu4-u2-1l.body: 不得不 'can't not' is a double negative: you have no choice but to, usually because of pressure from outside. It's stronger than 必须 and carries a note of reluctance. 只好 'have to, can only' is milder, for making the best of a situation after something has happened. Don't put 不 after 不得不: say 不得不去, not 不得不不去. 好的初中竞争那么激烈，我不得不早做准备。 (Competition for the good schools is so fierce that I've no choice but to prepare early.)

dabu4-u2-1l.title: 非 … 不可: simply have to
dabu4-u2-1l.body: 非…不可 'unless …, it won't do' means something must happen. It's emphatic, and often a little exasperated. With 要, 非要…不可 means someone insists on doing something, usually against advice; in speech the 不可 is often dropped: 他非要去. 孩子想上好大学，就非从小打好基础不可。 (If a child wants to get into a good university, they simply have to build the foundations early.)

dabu4-u2-5i.title: 尽管 … 还是 / 但是 …: even though
dabu4-u2-5i.body: 尽管 is a more written 虽然 'although', and it stresses that B happens in spite of A. The second clause usually has 但是 or 可是, and often 还是 or 也 before the verb. It's the natural way to concede a point in an essay before you make your own. 尽管国家出台了“双减”政策，家长还是很焦虑。 (Although the government introduced the 'double reduction' policy, parents are still anxious.)

dabu4-u2-4j.title: 凭 and 靠: on the strength of
dabu4-u2-4j.body: 凭 'on the strength of, by virtue of' names what you can rightfully count on: your score, your skill, your own work. 靠 from 大步 3 is broader, 'rely on', and can mean help from others. 凭什么？ 'on what grounds?' is a sharp challenge, and can sound rude, so save it for arguments you mean. 我能凭的，只有自己的分数。 (All I had to go on was my own score.)

dabu4-u2-2h.title: Culture · The gaokao, and the race that leads up to it
dabu4-u2-2h.body: The 高考, the national university entrance exam, starts every year on 7 June and lasts two to four days, depending on the province. In 2025 about 13.4 million people sat it. For most, the score decides which university, and often which city, they go to. Streets near exam halls go quiet, police escort latecomers, and parents wait outside the gates, some wearing red for luck. In 高三, the final year, many students study from early morning until late at night under a countdown on the classroom board.

dabu4-u3-2f.title: 与其说 … 不如说 …: it's not so much A as B
dabu4-u3-2f.body: 与其说A，不如说B re-describes something: 'rather than calling it A, it would be truer to call it B'. It corrects a label, not a choice, so it's different from 与其A，不如B 'better to do B than A' from 大步 1, which recommends an action. It's thoughtful and a little literary, and very useful when you want to change how someone sees a situation. 与其说姨父是怕花钱，不如说他是怕自己没用了。 (It isn't so much that Uncle's afraid of the cost as that he's afraid of being useless.)

dabu4-u3-6g.title: 固然 … 但是 …: admittedly
dabu4-u3-6g.body: 固然 grants a point fully, 'it's true that, of course', before the real argument comes with 但是 or 可是. It goes after the subject. It's written and measured, and it makes an argument sound fair, because you've shown you've thought about the other side first. 专业的护理固然代替不了儿女的陪伴，但是累垮了的儿女也照顾不好父母。 (Professional nursing can't take the place of children's company, of course, but children who are worn out can't care for their parents well either.)

dabu4-u3-8h.title: 哪怕 … 也 …: even if
dabu4-u3-8h.body: 哪怕 'even if, even though' is like 即使 from 大步 3, but more emotional and more common in speech: it often introduces an extreme or a small, humble case. 也 or 都 follows in the second clause. 哪怕是 + noun is common too: 哪怕是一个电话 'even just a phone call'. 哪怕不能天天在身边，多打一个电话也是孝顺。 (Even if you can't be there every day, one more phone call is duty too.)

dabu4-u3-2g.title: 照顾, 照料, 护理 and 陪: caring for someone
dabu4-u3-2g.body: 照顾 is the everyday word for looking after someone, and also for keeping an eye out for them. 照料 is its written twin, common in notices and reports (日间照料 'day care'). 护理 is nursing care, done by professionals. 陪 and 陪伴 are about company, being with someone, and that's what many older people want most. 她一个人照顾生病的丈夫。 (She's looking after her sick husband on her own.)

dabu4-u3-2g.title: Culture · Filial piety, and who cares for the old
dabu4-u3-2g.body: 孝, filial piety, has been at the heart of Chinese ethics for more than two thousand years. 孝顺 joins respect (孝) with going along with your parents' wishes (顺), and the old saying 养儿防老, 'raise children to provide for old age', assumed that sons and daughters would care for their parents at home. 'Face' (面子) matters too: for many older people, being seen to be looked after by their own children is a sign of a life well lived.

dabu4-u4-1g.title: Reporting speech in writing
dabu4-u4-1g.body: A profile mixes direct and indirect speech. Quote someone word for word with a colon and quotation marks, and keep their voice. Report them indirectly without quotation marks, changing 我 to 他 and 现在 to 那时. 据他回忆 'as he remembers it' marks his memory as the source; 用他的话说 introduces a phrase too good to paraphrase; 在他看来 gives his opinion. “那时候买什么都要票，”他说。 ('Back then you needed coupons for everything,' he says.)

dabu4-u4-1g.title: 回想起来 and 现在想想: looking back
dabu4-u4-1g.body: 回想起来 'thinking back on it' opens a reflection on the past from the present, and often leads to a judgement or a feeling you didn't have at the time. It's reflective and a little written. 现在想想 'thinking about it now' is its everyday equivalent. Both are followed by a comma. 现在回想起来，那是我最开心的时候。 (Looking back now, those were my happiest days.)

dabu4-u4-1g.title: 不由得 and 不禁: can't help it
dabu4-u4-1g.body: 不由得 'not up to you' means a reaction happens by itself, like 不禁 from 大步 2. 不由得 is a little more spoken, and it has a second use that 不禁 doesn't: 不由得你不信 'you can't help but believe it', with a person and 不 after it. Use either one sparingly: once in an essay is plenty. 我不由得想，他小时候的院子里有五个煤炉、二十多个人的声音。 (I couldn't help thinking that the courtyard of his childhood held five coal stoves and the voices of more than twenty people.)

dabu4-u4-5h.title: 与此同时: meanwhile
dabu4-u4-5h.body: 与此同时 'at the same time as this' links two things happening in parallel, usually one personal and one larger. It's written, and it opens the second sentence, followed by a comma. 同时 alone is more flexible and can go inside a clause. In a profile, 与此同时 is how you set one life against the history around it. 他进了纺织厂。与此同时，这个国家正在发生巨大的变化。 (He went into the textile mill. Meanwhile, the country was changing enormously.)

dabu4-u4-2h.title: Culture · Oral history, and one lifetime of change
dabu4-u4-2h.body: In the 1960s and 1970s most city families lived very close together. In Beijing, a courtyard house in a hutong that was built for one family was often shared by five or six households; in Shanghai, the same thing happened in the lane houses (石库门). Kitchens were shared, coal stoves (煤炉) were lit at the door each morning, and few homes had a toilet: Beijingers walked to the public one in the hutong, and in Shanghai the day began with emptying the chamber pot (倒马桶). Rice, oil, meat and cloth were rationed with coupons (票) from the 1950s until the early 1990s, and grain coupons were finally abolished in 1993. From 1968 until the late 1970s, some seventeen million young people from the cities were sent to the countryside (上山下乡) as 知青, 'educated youth'. Most came home around the end of the 1970s.

dabu5-u1-2h.title: Evidence or hearsay? 研究表明, 数据显示, 据说, 老话说
dabu5-u1-2h.body: When you talk about health, show how you know. 研究表明 'research shows' and 数据显示 'the data show' are for evidence, and belong in writing and careful speech. 据说 'it's said' and 听说 'I've heard' pass on something you haven't checked; 老话说 'as the old saying goes' quotes tradition. Mixing them up is how rumours sound like facts, so choose on purpose. 研究表明，骨头汤里的钙其实很少。 (Research shows there's very little calcium in bone soup.)

dabu5-u1-5i.title: 并非: it isn't so
dabu5-u1-5i.body: 并非 is the written form of 并不是: 'is not at all, is by no means'. It corrects an assumption firmly but calmly, which is why columns and reports love it. 也并非如此 'that isn't the case either' answers a question you've just raised. 并非都 means 'not all': 老话并非都是错的 'not all old sayings are wrong'. In speech, say 并不是 or 也不是. 老话并非都是错的。 (Not all old sayings are wrong.)

dabu5-u1-5i.title: 适当, 适量 and 过度: in moderation
dabu5-u1-5i.body: 适当 'appropriate, suitable' goes before verbs to mean 'a reasonable amount, when it's right': 适当运动, 适当休息. 适量 'a moderate amount' is for things you consume: food, drink, medicine, sun. 过度 'too much, excessive' is the opposite, and often comes before 劳累, 使用 or 治疗. All three are a little formal: a doctor's words. 空调开到二十六度，适当开窗通风。 (Set the air conditioning to twenty-six, and open the windows now and then.)

dabu5-u1-6i.title: 以…为主 and 因人而异
dabu5-u1-6i.body: 以A为主 'take A as the main thing' says what something mostly consists of: 饮食以清淡为主 'eat mostly light food'. It's neat and written, and very common in advice. 因人而异 'differs from person to person' is a four-character phrase for results that vary: use it to be honest about uncertain evidence. 夏天的饮食，最好以清淡为主。 (In summer, it's best to eat mostly light food.)

dabu5-u1-2i.title: Culture · The dog days, and the art of 'nourishing life'
dabu5-u1-2i.body: 养生, literally 'nourishing life', is an old idea: that you stay well through daily habits of eating, sleeping, moving and keeping calm, rather than waiting to be cured. It runs through traditional Chinese medicine (中医) and everyday speech. Older people swap tips in parks and group chats, and young office workers joke about 朋克养生, 'punk wellness': staying up till three, but with goji berries (枸杞) in the flask.

dabu5-u2-1i.title: 以偏概全 and 一概而论: don't generalise
dabu5-u2-1i.body: Two useful four-character phrases for pushing back on stereotypes. 以偏概全 'take a part for the whole' criticises a conclusion drawn from too little: one rude waiter, so all Londoners are rude. 一概而论 'treat everything the same way' is almost always negative: 不能一概而论 'you can't generalise'. Soften them with 有点儿 or 也, and they sound thoughtful rather than rude. “英国人都很冷漠”，就有点儿以偏概全了。 ('The English are all cold' is a bit of a sweeping generalisation.)

dabu5-u2-1i.title: 以为 or 认为?
dabu5-u2-1i.body: Both translate as 'think', but 以为 usually means you thought something that turned out to be wrong: 我以为中国菜都是甜的. 认为 states a considered opinion, and is more formal: 我认为旅行的意义在于交流. Don't use 以为 for a view you still hold, or it sounds as though you've changed your mind. 我以为中国人都很严肃，结果不是。 (I thought Chinese people were all serious, but they're not.)

dabu5-u2-2j.title: 对…而言: as far as … is concerned
dabu5-u2-2j.body: 对…而言 means 'for, as far as … is concerned', and is the written twin of 对…来说. It sets up whose point of view you're giving, often before a judgement about meaning or difficulty. 就…而言 is similar but narrows a topic rather than a person: 就价格而言 'in terms of price'. 对我而言，旅行最大的意义，就是把标签撕下来。 (For me, the biggest point of travelling is peeling off the labels.)

dabu5-u2-2j.title: …而已: that's all
dabu5-u2-2j.body: 而已 at the end of a sentence means 'and that's all, merely', and plays something down. It usually pairs with 只是, 不过 or 仅仅 earlier in the sentence. It's a little more written than 罢了, and it's a graceful way to be modest or to shrink an argument down to size. 其实，只是我听不懂而已。 (In fact, I just couldn't understand them, that's all.)

dabu5-u2-2i.title: Culture · Dunhuang and the Silk Road
dabu5-u2-2i.body: Dunhuang stands on the edge of the Gobi desert in Gansu, at the point where the old routes west divided to pass north and south of the Taklamakan. For more than a thousand years, merchants, monks, soldiers and envoys passed through it on the roads later named the Silk Road (丝绸之路). Silk, paper and porcelain went west; horses, glass, grapes, musical instruments like the pipa, and Buddhism came east.

dabu5-u3-6f.title: 一方面 … 另一方面 …: on the one hand, on the other
dabu5-u3-6f.body: 一方面…另一方面… sets out two aspects of one thing. In English 'on the one hand … on the other' usually contrasts; in Chinese the two sides often point the same way, adding one reason to another, though they can contrast too. The second half often takes 也 or 又. It's formal and balanced, and at home in essays, reports and meetings. 一方面，订单稳定；另一方面，也能学学人家的管理。 (On the one hand, the orders are steady; on the other, we can learn from how they're run.)

dabu5-u3-1i.title: 不可否认 and 然而: granting a point, then turning
dabu5-u3-1i.body: 不可否认 'it can't be denied' grants a point fully, and is stronger than 固然 from 大步 4. 然而 'however' is the written 可是: it opens a sentence or clause and turns the argument. Used together, they make a formal essay sound fair before it criticises. In speech you'd say 确实… and 可是…. 不可否认，这是个大机会。 (There's no denying it's a big opportunity.)

dabu5-u3-1i.title: 由此可见 and 总而言之: drawing a conclusion, and closing
dabu5-u3-1i.body: 由此可见 'from this it can be seen' draws a conclusion from the example or evidence just given; 可见 alone is lighter and can go mid-sentence. 总而言之 'to sum up' opens the final paragraph of an essay or the last point of a speech; 总之 is its everyday form. Don't use 由此可见 unless something really does follow. 由此可见，交流并不一定意味着失去自己。 (It follows that exchange doesn't necessarily mean losing yourself.)

dabu5-u3-4i.title: 以…为代价: at the cost of
dabu5-u3-4i.body: 以A为代价 'taking A as the price' says what is sacrificed to get something. It's written and usually critical, and often comes with 换取 'get in exchange' or 来. Use it to name the hidden cost of a gain: health for money, the environment for growth. 不少工厂以牺牲环境为代价，换取订单。 (Many factories win orders at the expense of the environment.)

dabu5-u3-2g.title: Culture · From 'Made in China' to the story behind it
dabu5-u3-2g.body: Since China opened up to world trade in the 1980s, and especially after it joined the World Trade Organization in 2001, 中国制造 'Made in China' has been printed on a large share of the world's goods. China became the world's biggest exporter of goods in 2009, and now accounts for around 14 per cent of global goods exports.

dabu5-u4-1h.title: Opening a speech: 尊敬的…, 亲爱的…, 大家好
dabu5-u4-1h.body: A Chinese speech opens by addressing the audience, most senior first, followed by a colon: 尊敬的 'respected' for guests, teachers or leaders, 亲爱的 'dear' for friends, and 各位 + group for everyone else. Then comes the greeting, and usually 首先 with a thank-you to whoever invited you. At an informal event, 各位朋友，大家好 is plenty. 尊敬的各位老师，亲爱的朋友们：大家下午好！ (Teachers, dear friends: good afternoon!)

dabu5-u4-3h.title: 如果说 … 那么 …: if A, then B
dabu5-u4-3h.body: 如果说A，那么B is not a real condition. It sets two things side by side, usually to build to the bigger one: 'if the first year gave me friends, then later it gave me homes'. It's a favourite of speeches and essays because it moves the argument up a step. Keep A and B parallel in shape. 如果说第一年，中文给了我几个朋友，那么后来，它给了我好几个家。 (If in the first year Chinese gave me a few friends, then later it gave me several homes.)

dabu5-u4-4k.title: Closing a speech: 最后, 感谢, 谢谢大家
dabu5-u4-4k.body: 最后 'finally' signals the end, and it's usually where the thanks go: 我要感谢 A，感谢 B…, with 感谢 repeated for each person. End with 谢谢大家 or 谢谢 on its own line, and at a festival or a party, a wish with 祝. 我的话就说到这里 'that's all from me' is a modest way to finish. 最后，我要感谢小雨，她是我的第一位中文老师。 (Finally, I'd like to thank Xiaoyu, my first Chinese teacher.)

dabu5-u4-3i.title: 成语 and sayings in a speech
dabu5-u4-3i.body: A 成语 or an old saying is at its best at a turning point: when it sums up what you've just said, or opens what you're about to say. Introduce a longer saying with 中国有句老话 or the person who said it, and put it in quotation marks. One or two in a speech is plenty. Some, like 一步一个脚印, work as adverbs with 地 before a verb. 中国有句老话：“千里之行，始于足下。” (There's an old Chinese saying: 'A journey of a thousand miles begins with a single step.')

dabu5-u4-2h.title: Culture · Sayings that open doors
dabu5-u4-2h.body: The first saying of the 《论语》, the Analects of Confucius, is about learning and friendship: 学而时习之，不亦说乎？有朋自远方来，不亦乐乎？ 'To learn, and practise what you have learned: is that not a pleasure? To have friends come from afar: is that not a joy?' Chinese hosts still quote the second line to welcome visitors, and it's printed on banners at airports, conferences and graduations.

turns.name: 小雨
turns.hanzi: 你好！请问，你是马克吗？
turns.pinyin: nǐhǎo! qǐngwèn, nǐ shì Mǎkè ma?
turns.en: Hello! Excuse me, are you Mark?

turns.name: 马克
turns.hanzi: 是，我是马克。你好！
turns.pinyin: shì, wǒ shì Mǎkè. nǐhǎo!
turns.en: Yes, I'm Mark. Hello!

turns.name: 小雨
turns.hanzi: 我叫林小雨。
turns.pinyin: wǒ jiào Línxiǎoyǔ.
turns.en: My name is Lin Xiaoyu.

turns.name: 马克
turns.hanzi: 你姓林吗？
turns.pinyin: nǐ xìng Lín ma?
turns.en: Is your surname Lin?

turns.name: 小雨
turns.hanzi: 对，我姓林。你姓什么？
turns.pinyin: duì, wǒ xìng Lín. nǐ xìng shénme?
turns.en: Yes, my surname is Lin. What's your surname?

turns.name: 马克
turns.hanzi: 我姓 Smith。
turns.pinyin: wǒ xìngSmith.
turns.en: My surname is Smith.

turns.name: 小雨
turns.hanzi: 很高兴认识你，马克！
turns.pinyin: hěn gāoxìng rènshi nǐ, Mǎkè!
turns.en: Nice to meet you, Mark!

turns.name: 马克
turns.hanzi: 我也很高兴认识你！
turns.pinyin: wǒ yě hěn gāoxìng rènshi nǐ!
turns.en: Nice to meet you too!

turns.name: 小雨
turns.hanzi: 朵朵，这是我朋友。
turns.pinyin: Duǒduo, zhè shì wǒ péngyou.
turns.en: Duoduo, this is my friend.

turns.name: 朵朵
turns.hanzi: 你好！我叫朵朵。你叫什么名字？
turns.pinyin: nǐhǎo! wǒ jiào Duǒduo. nǐ jiào shénme míngzi?
turns.en: Hi! I'm Duoduo. What's your name?

turns.name: 马克
turns.hanzi: 我叫马克。你是学生吗？
turns.pinyin: wǒ jiào Mǎkè. nǐ shì xuésheng ma?
turns.en: I'm Mark. Are you a student?

turns.name: 朵朵
turns.hanzi: 是，我是学生。你呢？
turns.pinyin: shì, wǒ shì xuésheng. nǐ ne?
turns.en: Yes, I'm a student. And you?

turns.name: 马克
turns.hanzi: 我不是学生。
turns.pinyin: wǒ bù shì xuésheng.
turns.en: I'm not a student.

turns.name: 小雨
turns.hanzi: 马克，你喝咖啡吗？
turns.pinyin: Mǎkè, nǐ hē kāfēi ma?
turns.en: Mark, will you have a coffee?

turns.name: 马克
turns.hanzi: 不喝，谢谢。我喝茶。
turns.pinyin: bù hē, xièxie. wǒ hē chá.
turns.en: No, thanks. I'll have tea.

turns.name: 朵朵
turns.hanzi: 我也喝茶！
turns.pinyin: wǒ yě hē chá!
turns.en: Tea for me too!

turns.name: 小雨
turns.hanzi: 马克，你是哪国人？
turns.pinyin: Mǎkè, nǐ shì nǎ guó rén?
turns.en: Mark, what nationality are you?

turns.name: 马克
turns.hanzi: 我是英国人，我住在伦敦。你呢？你从哪里来？
turns.pinyin: wǒ shì yīngguó rén, wǒ zhù zài lúndūn. nǐ ne? nǐ cóng nǎlǐ lái?
turns.en: I'm British. I live in London. And you? Where are you from?

turns.name: 小雨
turns.hanzi: 我从中国来。
turns.pinyin: wǒ cóng zhōngguó lái.
turns.en: I'm from China.

turns.name: 马克
turns.hanzi: 你是哪里人？
turns.pinyin: nǐ shì nǎlǐ rén?
turns.en: Which part of China?

turns.name: 小雨
turns.hanzi: 我是成都人。
turns.pinyin: wǒ shì chéngdū rén.
turns.en: I'm from Chengdu.

turns.name: 马克
turns.hanzi: 朵朵也是成都人吗？
turns.pinyin: Duǒduo yě shì chéngdū rén ma?
turns.en: Is Duoduo from Chengdu too?

turns.name: 小雨
turns.hanzi: 不是，她是英国人，也是中国人！她住在伦敦。
turns.pinyin: bù shì, tā shì yīngguó rén, yě shì zhōngguó rén! tā zhù zài lúndūn.
turns.en: No, she's British, and Chinese too! She lives in London.

turns.name: 马克
turns.hanzi: 朵朵，你会说英语吗？
turns.pinyin: Duǒduo, nǐ huì shuō yīngyǔ ma?
turns.en: Duoduo, can you speak English?

turns.name: 朵朵
turns.hanzi: 会！我会说英语和中文。你会说中文吗？
turns.pinyin: huì! wǒ huì shuō yīngyǔ hé zhōngwén. nǐ huì shuō zhōngwén ma?
turns.en: Yes! I speak English and Chinese. Can you speak Chinese?

turns.name: 马克
turns.hanzi: 我会说一点儿中文，也会说一点儿法语。
turns.pinyin: wǒ huì shuō yīdiǎnr zhōngwén, yě huì shuō yīdiǎnr fǎyǔ.
turns.en: I speak a little Chinese, and a little French too.

turns.name: 小雨
turns.hanzi: 我会说中文和英语，也会说一点儿日语。
turns.pinyin: wǒ huì shuō zhōngwén hé yīngyǔ, yě huì shuō yīdiǎnr rìyǔ.
turns.en: I speak Chinese and English, and a little Japanese too.

turns.name: 朵朵
turns.hanzi: 马克，你只会说一点儿中文！
turns.pinyin: Mǎkè, nǐ zhǐ huì shuō yīdiǎnr zhōngwén!
turns.en: Mark, you only speak a little Chinese!

turns.name: 小雨
turns.hanzi: 没关系！我们一起学！
turns.pinyin: méiguānxi! wǒmen yīqǐ xué!
turns.en: Never mind! We'll learn together!

turns.name: 小雨
turns.hanzi: 马克，你做什么工作？
turns.pinyin: Mǎkè, nǐ zuò shénme gōngzuò?
turns.en: Mark, what do you do?

turns.name: 马克
turns.hanzi: 我是设计师。
turns.pinyin: wǒ shì shèjìshī.
turns.en: I'm a designer.

turns.name: 小雨
turns.hanzi: 真的吗？我在大学学设计！
turns.pinyin: zhēnde ma? wǒ zài dàxué xué shèjì!
turns.en: Really? I study design at university!

turns.name: 马克
turns.hanzi: 太好了！你是大学生吗？
turns.pinyin: tàihǎole! nǐ shì dàxuéshēng ma?
turns.en: Great! So you're a university student?

turns.name: 小雨
turns.hanzi: 对。你在哪儿工作？
turns.pinyin: duì. nǐ zài nǎr gōngzuò?
turns.en: Yes. Where do you work?

turns.name: 马克
turns.hanzi: 我在设计公司工作。
turns.pinyin: wǒ zài shèjì gōngsī gōngzuò.
turns.en: I work at a design company.

turns.name: 小雨
turns.hanzi: 马克，这是我表哥，陈明。
turns.pinyin: Mǎkè, zhè shì wǒ biǎogē, Chénmíng.
turns.en: Mark, this is my cousin, Chen Ming.

turns.name: 陈明
turns.hanzi: 你好！很高兴认识你。
turns.pinyin: nǐhǎo! hěn gāoxìng rènshi nǐ.
turns.en: Hi! Nice to meet you.

turns.name: 马克
turns.hanzi: 你好！你也是学生吗？
turns.pinyin: nǐhǎo! nǐ yě shì xuésheng ma?
turns.en: Hi! Are you a student too?

turns.name: 陈明
turns.hanzi: 不是，我是厨师。那是我的饭馆。
turns.pinyin: bù shì, wǒ shì chúshī. nà shì wǒ de fànguǎn.
turns.en: No, I'm a chef. That's my restaurant, over there.

turns.name: 马克
turns.hanzi: 那是你的饭馆？太好了！你的饭馆叫什么名字？
turns.pinyin: nà shì nǐ de fànguǎn? tàihǎole! nǐ de fànguǎn jiào shénme míngzi?
turns.en: That's yours? Great! What's it called?

turns.name: 陈明
turns.hanzi: 叫“陈家饺子”。
turns.pinyin: jiào Chénjiājiǎozi.
turns.en: It's called Chen Family Dumplings.

turns.name: 小雨
turns.hanzi: 陈明的饺子很好吃！
turns.pinyin: Chénmíng de jiǎozi hěn hǎochī!
turns.en: Chen Ming's dumplings are delicious!

turns.name: 马克
turns.hanzi: 请问，这是谁的手机？
turns.pinyin: qǐngwèn, zhè shì shéi de shǒujī?
turns.en: Excuse me, whose phone is this?

turns.name: 陈明
turns.hanzi: 是我的，谢谢！
turns.pinyin: shì wǒ de, xièxie!
turns.en: It's mine, thanks!

dialogues.title: Let's add each other on WeChat!

turns.name: 马克
turns.hanzi: 小雨，我们加个微信吧！
turns.pinyin: Xiǎoyǔ, wǒmen jiā gè wēixìn ba!
turns.en: Xiaoyu, let's add each other on WeChat!

turns.name: 小雨
turns.hanzi: 好！你扫我的二维码吧。
turns.pinyin: hǎo! nǐ sǎo wǒ de èrwéimǎ ba.
turns.en: OK! Scan my QR code.

turns.name: 马克
turns.hanzi: 好。你的电话号码是多少？
turns.pinyin: hǎo. nǐ de diànhuà hàomǎ shì duōshǎo?
turns.en: OK. What's your phone number?

turns.name: 小雨
turns.hanzi: 零七七零零，九零零，四六幺。
turns.pinyin: líng qīqī línglíng, jiǔ línglíng, sìliù yāo.

turns.name: 马克
turns.hanzi: 零七七零零，九零零，四六一？
turns.pinyin: líng qīqī línglíng, jiǔ línglíng, sìliù yī?
turns.en: 07700 900… four six one?

turns.name: 小雨
turns.hanzi: 对！电话号码的“一”，我们说“幺”。
turns.pinyin: duì! diànhuà hàomǎ de yī, wǒmen shuō yāo.
turns.en: Yes! In phone numbers we say yāo for one.

turns.name: 马克
turns.hanzi: 我的是零七七零零，九零零，二三八。
turns.pinyin: wǒ de shì líng qīqī línglíng, jiǔ línglíng, èr sānbā.

turns.name: 马克
turns.hanzi: 陈明，你多大？
turns.pinyin: Chénmíng, nǐ duōdà?
turns.en: Chen Ming, how old are you?

turns.name: 陈明
turns.hanzi: 我三十二岁。你呢？
turns.pinyin: wǒ sān shí èr suì. nǐ ne?
turns.en: I'm 32. And you?

turns.name: 马克
turns.hanzi: 我二十八岁。朵朵，你几岁？
turns.pinyin: wǒ èr shí bā suì. Duǒduo, nǐ jǐ suì?
turns.en: I'm 28. Duoduo, how old are you?

turns.name: 朵朵
turns.hanzi: 我八岁！
turns.pinyin: wǒ bā suì!
turns.en: I'm eight!

turns.name: 马克
turns.hanzi: 陈明，你的饭馆有几个厨师？
turns.pinyin: Chénmíng, nǐ de fànguǎn yǒu jǐ gè chúshī?
turns.en: Chen Ming, how many chefs are there at your restaurant?

turns.name: 陈明
turns.hanzi: 有三个厨师，两个服务员。
turns.pinyin: yǒu sān gè chúshī, liǎng gè fúwùyuán.
turns.en: Three chefs and two waiters.

turns.name: 马克
turns.hanzi: 你们一天做多少饺子？
turns.pinyin: nǐmen yī tiān zuò duōshǎo jiǎozi?
turns.en: How many dumplings do you make a day?

turns.name: 陈明
turns.hanzi: 差不多一千个！
turns.pinyin: chàbuduō yī qiān gè!
turns.en: About a thousand!

turns.name: 马克
turns.hanzi: 一千个！太多了！
turns.pinyin: yī qiān gè! tài duō le!
turns.en: A thousand! That's so many!

turns.name: 小雨
turns.hanzi: 马克，你在干什么呢？
turns.pinyin: Mǎkè, nǐ zài gàn shénme ne?
turns.en: Mark, what are you up to?

turns.name: 马克
turns.hanzi: 我在学中文呢！你呢？
turns.pinyin: wǒ zài xué zhōngwén ne! nǐ ne?
turns.en: I'm studying Chinese! And you?

turns.name: 小雨
turns.hanzi: 我在家听音乐。
turns.pinyin: wǒ zài jiā tīng yīnyuè.
turns.en: I'm at home listening to music.

turns.name: 马克
turns.hanzi: 陈明呢？他在做饭吗？
turns.pinyin: Chénmíng ne? tā zài zuòfàn ma?
turns.en: What about Chen Ming? Is he cooking?

turns.name: 小雨
turns.hanzi: 对，他在饭馆做饺子。
turns.pinyin: duì, tā zài fànguǎn zuò jiǎozi.
turns.en: Yes, he's making dumplings at the restaurant.

turns.name: 马克
turns.hanzi: 他的饺子太好吃了！
turns.pinyin: tā de jiǎozi tài hǎochī le!
turns.en: His dumplings are so good!

turns.name: 小雨
turns.hanzi: 明天晚上你想做什么？
turns.pinyin: míngtiān wǎnshang nǐ xiǎng zuò shénme?
turns.en: What do you want to do tomorrow evening?

turns.name: 马克
turns.hanzi: 我想看电影。你呢？
turns.pinyin: wǒ xiǎng kàn diànyǐng. nǐ ne?
turns.en: I'd like to see a film. You?

turns.name: 小雨
turns.hanzi: 我要去陈明的饭馆吃饺子。你想去吗？
turns.pinyin: wǒ yào qù Chénmíng de fànguǎn chī jiǎozi. nǐ xiǎng qù ma?
turns.en: I'm going to Chen Ming's restaurant for dumplings. Do you want to come?

turns.name: 马克
turns.hanzi: 想！我们一起去吧！
turns.pinyin: xiǎng! wǒmen yīqǐ qù ba!
turns.en: Yes! Let's go together!

turns.name: 小雨
turns.hanzi: 太好了！明天见！
turns.pinyin: tàihǎole! míngtiānjiàn!
turns.en: Great! See you tomorrow!

turns.name: 马克
turns.hanzi: 明天见！
turns.pinyin: míngtiānjiàn!
turns.en: See you tomorrow!

turns.name: 小雨
turns.hanzi: 马克，你周末喜欢做什么？
turns.pinyin: Mǎkè, nǐ zhōumò xǐhuan zuò shénme?
turns.en: Mark, what do you like doing at the weekend?

turns.name: 马克
turns.hanzi: 我喜欢做饭，也喜欢逛市场。你有什么爱好？
turns.pinyin: wǒ xǐhuan zuòfàn, yě xǐhuan guàng shìchǎng. nǐ yǒu shénme àihào?
turns.en: I like cooking, and I like wandering round markets. What are your hobbies?

turns.name: 小雨
turns.hanzi: 我很喜欢音乐。我喜欢唱歌，也喜欢弹吉他。
turns.pinyin: wǒ hěn xǐhuan yīnyuè. wǒ xǐhuan chànggē, yě xǐhuan tán jítā.
turns.en: I love music. I like singing, and playing the guitar.

turns.name: 马克
turns.hanzi: 星期六你有空吗？我们一起去逛博罗市场吧！
turns.pinyin: xīngqī liù nǐ yǒukòng ma? wǒmen yīqǐ qù guàng Bóluóshìchǎng ba!
turns.en: Are you free on Saturday? Let's go to Borough Market!

turns.name: 小雨
turns.hanzi: 好啊！表哥，你也一起去吧？
turns.pinyin: hǎo a! biǎogē, nǐ yě yīqǐ qù ba?
turns.en: Sure! You'll come too, won't you, cousin?

turns.name: 陈明
turns.hanzi: 星期六？不好意思，星期六饭馆很忙，我要工作。
turns.pinyin: xīngqī liù? bùhǎoyìsi, xīngqī liù fànguǎn hěn máng, wǒ yào gōngzuò.
turns.en: Saturday? Sorry, Saturday's busy at the restaurant. I have to work.

turns.name: 马克
turns.hanzi: 那星期天呢？你有空吗？
turns.pinyin: nà xīngqītiān ne? nǐ yǒukòng ma?
turns.en: What about Sunday, then? Are you free?

turns.name: 陈明
turns.hanzi: 星期天上午可以。
turns.pinyin: xīngqītiān shàngwǔ kěyǐ.
turns.en: Sunday morning's fine.

turns.name: 小雨
turns.hanzi: 那我们星期天上午去，怎么样？
turns.pinyin: nà wǒmen xīngqītiān shàngwǔ qù, zěnmeyàng?
turns.en: Then let's go on Sunday morning. How's that?

turns.name: 马克
turns.hanzi: 好主意！
turns.pinyin: hǎozhǔyi!
turns.en: Good idea!

dialogues.title: What did you do last weekend?

turns.name: 陈妈妈
turns.hanzi: 马克，上个周末你做了什么？
turns.pinyin: Mǎkè, shàng gè zhōumò nǐ zuò le shénme?
turns.en: Mark, what did you do last weekend?

turns.name: 马克
turns.hanzi: 星期天我和小雨、陈明去了博罗市场。
turns.pinyin: xīngqītiān wǒ hé Xiǎoyǔ, Chénmíng qù le Bóluóshìchǎng.
turns.en: On Sunday I went to Borough Market with Xiaoyu and Chen Ming.

turns.name: 陈妈妈
turns.hanzi: 真的吗？你们买了什么？
turns.pinyin: zhēnde ma? nǐmen mǎi le shénme?
turns.en: Really? What did you buy?

turns.name: 马克
turns.hanzi: 我买了一些面包和水果，陈明买了很多菜。
turns.pinyin: wǒ mǎi le yīxiē miànbāo hé shuǐguǒ, Chénmíng mǎi le hěnduō cài.
turns.en: I bought some bread and fruit, and Chen Ming bought loads of vegetables.

turns.name: 陈妈妈
turns.hanzi: 小雨呢？
turns.pinyin: Xiǎoyǔ ne?
turns.en: And Xiaoyu?

turns.name: 马克
turns.hanzi: 她没买东西，可是拍了很多照片！你们呢？周末做了什么？
turns.pinyin: tā méi mǎi dōngxi, kěshì pāi le hěnduō zhàopiàn! nǐmen ne? zhōumò zuò le shénme?
turns.en: She didn't buy anything, but she took loads of photos! What about you? What did you do at the weekend?

turns.name: 陈妈妈
turns.hanzi: 我和朵朵在家做了几个北京菜，还看了一个电影。
turns.pinyin: wǒ hé Duǒduo zài jiā zuò le jǐ gè běijīng cài, hái kàn le yī gè diànyǐng.
turns.en: Duoduo and I cooked a few Beijing dishes at home, and watched a film.

turns.name: 马克
turns.hanzi: 北京菜！下次请我吃吧！
turns.pinyin: běijīng cài! xià cì qǐng wǒ chī ba!
turns.en: Beijing food! Invite me next time!

turns.name: 陈妈妈
turns.hanzi: 可以啊！
turns.pinyin: kěyǐ a!
turns.en: Sure!

dialogues.title: What time do you get up?

turns.name: 小雨
turns.hanzi: 马克，你每天几点起床？
turns.pinyin: Mǎkè, nǐ měitiān jǐ diǎn qǐchuáng?
turns.en: Mark, what time do you get up every day?

turns.name: 马克
turns.hanzi: 七点半。八点一刻出门，九点上班。
turns.pinyin: qī diǎn bàn. bā diǎn yī kè chūmén, jiǔ diǎn shàngbān.
turns.en: Half past seven. I leave home at quarter past eight and start work at nine.

turns.name: 小雨
turns.hanzi: 你几点下班？
turns.pinyin: nǐ jǐ diǎn xiàbān?
turns.en: What time do you finish work?

turns.name: 马克
turns.hanzi: 差不多六点。下班以后，我常常去跑步。你呢？
turns.pinyin: chàbuduō liù diǎn. xiàbān yǐhòu, wǒ chángcháng qù pǎobù. nǐ ne?
turns.en: About six. After work I often go running. And you?

turns.name: 小雨
turns.hanzi: 我每天上午都有课。中午在学校吃午饭，下午去图书馆。
turns.pinyin: wǒ měitiān shàngwǔ dōu yǒu kè. zhōngwǔ zài xuéxiào chī wǔfàn, xiàwǔ qù túshūguǎn.
turns.en: I have classes every morning. I have lunch at university at midday, and in the afternoon I go to the library.

turns.name: 马克
turns.hanzi: 你晚上几点睡觉？
turns.pinyin: nǐ wǎnshang jǐ diǎn shuìjiào?
turns.en: What time do you go to bed?

turns.name: 小雨
turns.hanzi: 十二点以后。你呢？
turns.pinyin: shí èr diǎn yǐhòu. nǐ ne?
turns.en: After twelve. And you?

turns.name: 马克
turns.hanzi: 十一点。睡觉以前，我喜欢看一点儿书。
turns.pinyin: shí yī diǎn. shuìjiào yǐqián, wǒ xǐhuan kàn yīdiǎnr shū.
turns.en: Eleven. Before bed I like to read a bit.

turns.name: 小雨
turns.hanzi: 周末呢？
turns.pinyin: zhōumò ne?
turns.en: What about weekends?

turns.name: 马克
turns.hanzi: 周末不上班，上午常常在家休息。
turns.pinyin: zhōumò bù shàngbān, shàngwǔ chángcháng zài jiā xiūxi.
turns.en: I don't work at weekends, so I usually take it easy at home in the morning.

turns.name: 小雨
turns.hanzi: 马克，你在哪儿？现在已经两点十分了！
turns.pinyin: Mǎkè, nǐ zài nǎr? xiànzài yǐjīng liǎng diǎn shí fēn le!
turns.en: Mark, where are you? It's already ten past two!

turns.name: 马克
turns.hanzi: 对不起！我在地铁上，地铁晚点了。
turns.pinyin: duìbuqǐ! wǒ zài dìtiě shang, dìtiě wǎndiǎn le.
turns.en: Sorry! I'm on the Tube, and it's running late.

turns.name: 小雨
turns.hanzi: 你什么时候到？电影两点四十五开始。
turns.pinyin: nǐ shénmeshíhou dào? diànyǐng liǎng diǎn sìshíwǔ kāishǐ.
turns.en: When will you get here? The film starts at quarter to three.

turns.name: 马克
turns.hanzi: 二十分钟以后到，两点半吧。
turns.pinyin: èr shí fēnzhōng yǐhòu dào, liǎng diǎn bàn ba.
turns.en: In twenty minutes. Half past two, I think.

turns.name: 小雨
turns.hanzi: 好吧。我先去买票，在电影院门口等你。一会儿见！
turns.pinyin: hǎo ba. wǒ xiān qù mǎi piào, zài diànyǐngyuàn ménkǒu děng nǐ. yīhuìr jiàn!
turns.en: OK. I'll go and get the tickets, and wait for you outside the cinema. See you in a bit!

turns.name: 马克
turns.hanzi: 小雨！我来了！现在几点？
turns.pinyin: Xiǎoyǔ! wǒ lái le! xiànzài jǐ diǎn?
turns.en: Xiaoyu! I'm here! What time is it?

turns.name: 小雨
turns.hanzi: 差五分三点！电影已经开始了，快走吧！
turns.pinyin: chà wǔ fēn sān diǎn! diànyǐng yǐjīng kāishǐ le, kuài zǒu ba!
turns.en: Five to three! The film's already started. Come on, quick!

turns.name: 马克
turns.hanzi: 对不起，对不起！晚上我请你吃饭！
turns.pinyin: duìbuqǐ, duìbuqǐ! wǎnshang wǒ qǐng nǐ chīfàn!
turns.en: Sorry, sorry! Dinner's on me tonight!

turns.name: 陈妈妈
turns.hanzi: 你们好！想喝点儿什么？
turns.pinyin: nǐmen hǎo! xiǎng hē diǎnr shénme?
turns.en: Hello, you two! What would you like?

turns.name: 小雨
turns.hanzi: 我要一杯珍珠奶茶，少糖。
turns.pinyin: wǒ yào yī bēi zhēnzhū nǎichá, shǎo táng.
turns.en: I'll have a pearl milk tea, less sugar.

turns.name: 陈妈妈
turns.hanzi: 大杯还是中杯？
turns.pinyin: dà bēi háishi zhōng bēi?
turns.en: Large or medium?

turns.name: 小雨
turns.hanzi: 大杯。马克，你喝哪个？
turns.pinyin: dà bēi. Mǎkè, nǐ hē nǎge?
turns.en: Large. Mark, which one are you having?

turns.name: 马克
turns.hanzi: 这个是什么？
turns.pinyin: zhège shì shénme?
turns.en: What's this one?

turns.name: 小雨
turns.hanzi: 那个是芒果绿茶，很好喝。
turns.pinyin: nàge shì mángguǒ lǜchá, hěn hǎohē.
turns.en: That's mango green tea. It's really nice.

turns.name: 马克
turns.hanzi: 那我要一杯芒果绿茶，中杯，不要冰。
turns.pinyin: nà wǒ yào yī bēi mángguǒ lǜchá, zhōng bēi, bù yào bīng.
turns.en: Then I'll have a mango green tea, medium, no ice.

turns.name: 陈妈妈
turns.hanzi: 好的。还要别的吗？
turns.pinyin: hǎode. hái yào biéde ma?
turns.en: OK. Anything else?

turns.name: 马克
turns.hanzi: 还要两个蛋挞。
turns.pinyin: hái yào liǎng gè dàntà.
turns.en: And two egg tarts, please.

turns.name: 陈妈妈
turns.hanzi: 好的，请等一下。
turns.pinyin: hǎode, qǐng děng yīxià.
turns.en: Sure, just a moment.

turns.name: 陈明
turns.hanzi: 可乐要十瓶，果汁要五瓶。
turns.pinyin: kělè yào shí píng, guǒzhī yào wǔ píng.
turns.en: We need ten bottles of cola and five of juice.

turns.name: 马克
turns.hanzi: 月饼呢？买几盒？
turns.pinyin: yuèbǐng ne? mǎi jǐ hé?
turns.en: What about mooncakes? How many boxes?

turns.name: 陈明
turns.hanzi: 六盒吧。你看，这张卡怎么样？
turns.pinyin: liù hé ba. nǐ kàn, zhè zhāng kǎ zěnmeyàng?
turns.en: Six, I think. Look, what do you think of this card?

turns.name: 马克
turns.hanzi: 很好看！是给谁的？
turns.pinyin: hěn hǎokàn! shì gěi shéi de?
turns.en: It's lovely! Who's it for?

turns.name: 陈明
turns.hanzi: 给小雨的。中秋节那天也是她的生日！
turns.pinyin: gěi Xiǎoyǔ de. zhōngqiūjié nà tiān yě shì tā de shēngrì!
turns.en: Xiaoyu. Her birthday's on Mid-Autumn this year!

turns.name: 马克
turns.hanzi: 真的吗？那我也要送她一件礼物。送什么好呢？
turns.pinyin: zhēnde ma? nà wǒ yě yào sòng tā yī jiàn lǐwù. sòng shénme hǎo ne?
turns.en: Really? Then I want to get her a present too. What should I give her?

turns.name: 陈明
turns.hanzi: 她喜欢音乐，送她一张唱片吧！
turns.pinyin: tā xǐhuan yīnyuè, sòng tā yī zhāng chàngpiàn ba!
turns.en: She loves music. Get her a record!

turns.name: 马克
turns.hanzi: 好主意！那条街上有一家唱片店。
turns.pinyin: hǎozhǔyi! nà tiáo jiē shang yǒu yī jiā chàngpiàn diàn.
turns.en: Good idea! There's a record shop on that street.

turns.name: 陈明
turns.hanzi: 别告诉小雨！
turns.pinyin: bié gàosu Xiǎoyǔ!
turns.en: Don't tell Xiaoyu!

turns.name: 马克
turns.hanzi: 放心吧！
turns.pinyin: fàngxīn ba!
turns.en: Don't worry!

turns.name: 小雨
turns.hanzi: 马克，下个星期五是中秋节。
turns.pinyin: Mǎkè, xià gè xīngqī wǔ shì zhōngqiūjié.
turns.en: Mark, next Friday is the Mid-Autumn Festival.

turns.name: 马克
turns.hanzi: 几月几号？
turns.pinyin: jǐ yuè jǐ hào?
turns.en: What's the date?

turns.name: 小雨
turns.hanzi: 九月二十五号。你打算怎么过？
turns.pinyin: jiǔ yuè èrshíwǔ hào. nǐ dǎsuàn zěnme guò?
turns.en: The twenty-fifth of September. How are you going to spend it?

turns.name: 马克
turns.hanzi: 我还不知道。你呢？
turns.pinyin: wǒ hái bù zhīdào. nǐ ne?
turns.en: I don't know yet. What about you?

turns.name: 小雨
turns.hanzi: 那天晚上，表哥的饭馆有个中秋节派对。你也来吧！
turns.pinyin: nà tiān wǎnshang, biǎogē de fànguǎn yǒu gè zhōngqiūjié pàiduì. nǐ yě lái ba!
turns.en: My cousin's restaurant is having a Mid-Autumn party that evening. Come along!

turns.name: 马克
turns.hanzi: 好啊！我下班以后去。对了，你的生日是几月几号？
turns.pinyin: hǎo a! wǒ xiàbān yǐhòu qù. duìle, nǐ de shēngrì shì jǐ yuè jǐ hào?
turns.en: Great! I'll come after work. Oh, by the way, when's your birthday?

turns.name: 小雨
turns.hanzi: 我的生日？……也是九月二十五号。
turns.pinyin: wǒ de shēngrì? yě shì jiǔ yuè èrshíwǔ hào.
turns.en: My birthday? ...It's the twenty-fifth of September too.

turns.name: 马克
turns.hanzi: 真的吗？太巧了！
turns.pinyin: zhēnde ma? tài qiǎo le!
turns.en: Really? What a coincidence!

turns.name: 小雨
turns.hanzi: 明年中秋节，我打算回成都，和家人一起过。
turns.pinyin: míngnián zhōngqiūjié, wǒ dǎsuàn huí chéngdū, hé jiārén yīqǐ guò.
turns.en: Next year I'm planning to go back to Chengdu for Mid-Autumn, and spend it with my family.

turns.name: 马克
turns.hanzi: 那今年我们在伦敦一起过！
turns.pinyin: nà jīnnián wǒmen zài lúndūn yīqǐ guò!
turns.en: Then this year we'll celebrate together in London!

turns.name: 陈明
turns.hanzi: 大家好！今天是中秋节，祝大家中秋节快乐！
turns.pinyin: dàjiā hǎo! jīntiān shì zhōngqiūjié, zhù dàjiā zhōngqiūjié kuàilè!
turns.en: Hello, everyone! Today's Mid-Autumn. Happy Mid-Autumn, everyone!

turns.name: 陈爸爸
turns.hanzi: 中秋节快乐！
turns.pinyin: zhōngqiūjié kuàilè!
turns.en: Happy Mid-Autumn!

turns.name: 陈明
turns.hanzi: 今天也是小雨的生日！小雨，生日快乐！
turns.pinyin: jīntiān yě shì Xiǎoyǔ de shēngrì! Xiǎoyǔ, shēngrì kuàilè!
turns.en: And today is Xiaoyu's birthday too! Happy birthday, Xiaoyu!

turns.name: 小雨
turns.hanzi: 啊？你们都知道？谢谢你们！
turns.pinyin: a? nǐmen dōu zhīdào? xièxie nǐmen!
turns.en: What? You all knew? Thank you!

turns.name: 马克
turns.hanzi: 小雨，这是我送你的生日礼物。
turns.pinyin: Xiǎoyǔ, zhè shì wǒ sòng nǐ de shēngrì lǐwù.
turns.en: Xiaoyu, this is my birthday present for you.

turns.name: 小雨
turns.hanzi: 一张唱片！太好了，谢谢你，马克！
turns.pinyin: yī zhāng chàngpiàn! tàihǎole, xièxie nǐ, Mǎkè!
turns.en: A record! Brilliant, thank you, Mark!

turns.name: 朵朵
turns.hanzi: 小雨，你今年多大？
turns.pinyin: Xiǎoyǔ, nǐ jīnnián duōdà?
turns.en: Xiaoyu, how old are you this year?

turns.name: 小雨
turns.hanzi: 二十三岁了！
turns.pinyin: èr shí sān suì le!
turns.en: Twenty-three!

turns.name: 陈妈妈
turns.hanzi: 快来吃蛋糕吧！还有月饼！
turns.pinyin: kuài lái chī dàngāo ba! hái yǒu yuèbǐng!
turns.en: Come and have some cake! There are mooncakes too!

turns.name: 朵朵
turns.hanzi: 你们看，今天晚上的月亮真圆！
turns.pinyin: nǐmen kàn, jīntiān wǎnshang de yuèliang zhēn yuán!
turns.en: Look, the moon's so round tonight!

turns.name: 马克
turns.hanzi: 小雨，你看新闻了吗？明天地铁罢工！
turns.pinyin: Xiǎoyǔ, nǐ kàn xīnwén le ma? míngtiān dìtiě bàgōng!
turns.en: Xiaoyu, have you seen the news? The Tube's on strike tomorrow!

turns.name: 小雨
turns.hanzi: 真的吗？那你明天怎么去上班？
turns.pinyin: zhēnde ma? nà nǐ míngtiān zěnme qù shàngbān?
turns.en: Really? So how are you going to get to work tomorrow?

turns.name: 马克
turns.hanzi: 我打算骑自行车去。
turns.pinyin: wǒ dǎsuàn qí zìxíngchē qù.
turns.en: I'm planning to cycle.

turns.name: 小雨
turns.hanzi: 从你家到公司要多长时间？
turns.pinyin: cóng nǐ jiā dào gōngsī yào duōchángshíjiān?
turns.en: How long does it take from your place to the office?

turns.name: 马克
turns.hanzi: 坐地铁要半个小时，骑车差不多要四十分钟。你呢？
turns.pinyin: zuò dìtiě yào bàn gè xiǎoshí, qíchē chàbuduō yào sì shí fēnzhōng. nǐ ne?
turns.en: It's half an hour on the Tube, and about forty minutes by bike. What about you?

turns.name: 小雨
turns.hanzi: 我每天坐公交车去学校，不坐地铁。
turns.pinyin: wǒ měitiān zuò gōngjiāochē qù xuéxiào, bù zuò dìtiě.
turns.en: I take the bus to college every day. I don't use the Tube.

turns.name: 马克
turns.hanzi: 陈明呢？他每天怎么去饭馆？
turns.pinyin: Chénmíng ne? tā měitiān zěnme qù fànguǎn?
turns.en: What about Chen Ming? How does he get to the restaurant?

turns.name: 小雨
turns.hanzi: 他走路去，只要十分钟。
turns.pinyin: tā zǒulù qù, zhǐ yào shí fēnzhōng.
turns.en: He walks. It only takes ten minutes.

turns.name: 马克
turns.hanzi: 那明天他没问题！
turns.pinyin: nà míngtiān tā méiwèntí!
turns.en: So he'll be fine tomorrow!

turns.name: 小雨
turns.hanzi: 对。你骑车小心点儿，路上车很多！
turns.pinyin: duì. nǐ qíchē xiǎoxīn diǎnr, lù shangchē hěnduō!
turns.en: Yes. Be careful on your bike, there's lots of traffic!

turns.name: 朵朵
turns.hanzi: 爸爸，下个周末我想去牛津。你们去过牛津吗？
turns.pinyin: bàba, xià gè zhōumò wǒ xiǎng qù Niújīn. nǐmen qù guo Niújīn ma?
turns.en: Dad, I'd like to go to Oxford next weekend. Have you been?

turns.name: 马克
turns.hanzi: 我去过好几次。牛津很漂亮！
turns.pinyin: wǒ qù guo hǎojǐ cì. Niújīn hěn piàoliang!
turns.en: I've been quite a few times. Oxford's beautiful!

turns.name: 朵朵
turns.hanzi: 从伦敦到牛津怎么去？
turns.pinyin: cóng lúndūn dào Niújīn zěnme qù?
turns.en: How do you get from London to Oxford?

turns.name: 马克
turns.hanzi: 坐火车一个小时左右。也可以坐大巴，要两个小时。
turns.pinyin: zuò huǒchē yī gè xiǎoshí zuǒyòu. yě kěyǐ zuò dàbā, yào liǎng gè xiǎoshí.
turns.en: It's about an hour by train. You can get the coach too, but that takes two hours.

turns.name: 陈明
turns.hanzi: 开车也很方便。马克，你会开车吗？
turns.pinyin: kāichē yě hěn fāngbiàn. Mǎkè, nǐ huì kāichē ma?
turns.en: Driving's easy too. Mark, can you drive?

turns.name: 马克
turns.hanzi: 会，可是我没有车。你呢？你去过牛津吗？
turns.pinyin: huì, kěshì wǒ méiyǒu chē. nǐ ne? nǐ qù guo Niújīn ma?
turns.en: Yes, but I haven't got a car. What about you? Have you been to Oxford?

turns.name: 陈明
turns.hanzi: 我有车，可是没去过牛津。我在伦敦住了十年，还没去过！
turns.pinyin: wǒ yǒu chē, kěshì méi qù guo Niújīn. wǒ zài lúndūn zhù le shí nián, hái méi qù guo!
turns.en: I've got a car, but I've never been. Ten years in London and I still haven't been!

turns.name: 朵朵
turns.hanzi: 那我们一起开车去吧！
turns.pinyin: nà wǒmen yīqǐ kāichē qù ba!
turns.en: Then let's all drive there together!

turns.name: 陈明
turns.hanzi: 好啊！星期天我有空。
turns.pinyin: hǎo a! xīngqītiān wǒ yǒukòng.
turns.en: Sure! I'm free on Sunday.

turns.name: 小雨
turns.hanzi: 今天有点儿冷！
turns.pinyin: jīntiān yǒudiǎnr lěng!
turns.en: It's a bit cold today!

turns.name: 马克
turns.hanzi: 冷吗？今天十二度，比昨天暖和一点儿。
turns.pinyin: lěng ma? jīntiān shí èr dù, bǐ zuótiān nuǎnhuo yīdiǎnr.
turns.en: Is it? It's twelve degrees, a bit warmer than yesterday.

turns.name: 小雨
turns.hanzi: 成都现在比伦敦暖和，差不多二十度。
turns.pinyin: chéngdū xiànzài bǐ lúndūn nuǎnhuo, chàbuduō èr shí dù.
turns.en: Chengdu's warmer than London at the moment, about twenty degrees.

turns.name: 马克
turns.hanzi: 成都的冬天冷吗？
turns.pinyin: chéngdū de dōngtiān lěng ma?
turns.en: Are winters cold in Chengdu?

turns.name: 小雨
turns.hanzi: 不太冷，没有北京那么冷。伦敦冬天常常下雪吗？
turns.pinyin: bù tài lěng, méiyǒu běijīng nàme lěng. lúndūn dōngtiān chángcháng xiàxuě ma?
turns.en: Not very. Not as cold as Beijing. Does it snow much in London in winter?

turns.name: 马克
turns.hanzi: 很少下雪，可是常常下雨。都是小雨！
turns.pinyin: hěn shǎo xiàxuě, kěshì chángcháng xiàyǔ. dōu shì Xiǎoyǔ!
turns.en: Hardly ever, but it rains a lot. Always light rain, xiǎoyǔ!

turns.name: 小雨
turns.hanzi: 小雨很好啊！成都也常常是阴天。你知道吗？伦敦的晴天比成都多！
turns.pinyin: Xiǎoyǔ hěn hǎo a! chéngdū yě chángcháng shì yīntiān. nǐ zhīdào ma? lúndūn de qíngtiān bǐ chéngdū duō!
turns.en: Xiǎoyǔ is lovely! Chengdu's often grey too. Did you know London gets more sunny days than Chengdu?

turns.name: 马克
turns.hanzi: 真的吗？伦敦的晴天比成都多？
turns.pinyin: zhēnde ma? lúndūn de qíngtiān bǐ chéngdū duō?
turns.en: Really? London has more sunny days than Chengdu?

turns.name: 小雨
turns.hanzi: 真的！所以成都人特别喜欢晒太阳。有太阳的时候，大家都去外面喝茶。
turns.pinyin: zhēnde! suǒyǐ chéngdū rén tèbié xǐhuan shàitàiyáng. yǒu tàiyáng de shíhou, dàjiā dōu qù wàimiàn hē chá.
turns.en: Really! That's why people in Chengdu love sitting in the sun. When the sun's out, everyone goes and drinks tea outside.

turns.name: 陈明
turns.hanzi: 小雨，你尝一下，这是我做的麻婆豆腐。
turns.pinyin: Xiǎoyǔ, nǐ cháng yīxià, zhè shì wǒ zuò de Mápódòufu.
turns.en: Xiaoyu, have a taste. This is my mapo tofu.

turns.name: 小雨
turns.hanzi: 好吃！可是没有成都的那么辣。
turns.pinyin: hǎochī! kěshì méiyǒu chéngdū de nàme là.
turns.en: It's good! But it's not as spicy as in Chengdu.

turns.name: 陈明
turns.hanzi: 我是北京人啊！北京菜没有四川菜那么辣。
turns.pinyin: wǒ shì běijīng rén a! běijīng cài méiyǒu sìchuān cài nàme là.
turns.en: I'm from Beijing! Beijing food isn't as spicy as Sichuan food.

turns.name: 马克
turns.hanzi: 这个已经很辣了！水！我要水！
turns.pinyin: zhège yǐjīng hěn là le! shuǐ! wǒ yào shuǐ!
turns.en: This is already really hot! Water! I need water!

turns.name: 小雨
turns.hanzi: 马克，这个一点儿也不辣！
turns.pinyin: Mǎkè, zhège yīdiǎnr yěbù là!
turns.en: Mark, this isn't spicy at all!

turns.name: 陈明
turns.hanzi: 马克，你怕辣吗？
turns.pinyin: Mǎkè, nǐ pà là ma?
turns.en: Mark, can't you handle chilli?

turns.name: 马克
turns.hanzi: 有点儿怕。英国菜不辣，可是英国人很喜欢吃咖喱。
turns.pinyin: yǒudiǎnr pà. yīngguó cài bù là, kěshì yīngguó rén hěn xǐhuan chī gālí.
turns.en: Not really. British food isn't spicy, but British people love curry.

turns.name: 小雨
turns.hanzi: 我妈妈做的菜更辣，也更好吃！
turns.pinyin: wǒ māma zuò de cài gèng là, yě gèng hǎochī!
turns.en: My mum's cooking is even spicier, and even tastier!

turns.name: 陈明
turns.hanzi: 什么？比我做的好吃？
turns.pinyin: shénme? bǐ wǒ zuò de hǎochī?
turns.en: What? Tastier than mine?

turns.name: 小雨
turns.hanzi: 一样好吃，一样好吃！
turns.pinyin: yīyàng hǎochī, yīyàng hǎochī!
turns.en: Just as good, just as good!

turns.name: 陈妈妈
turns.hanzi: 这是哪儿？唐人街往哪儿走？
turns.pinyin: zhè shì nǎr? Tángrénjiē wǎng nǎr zǒu?
turns.en: Where are we? Which way is Chinatown?

turns.name: 马克
turns.hanzi: 阿姨！叔叔！你们去唐人街吗？
turns.pinyin: āyí! shūshu! nǐmen qù Tángrénjiē ma?
turns.en: Auntie! Uncle! Are you going to Chinatown?

turns.name: 陈妈妈
turns.hanzi: 马克！太好了！请问，唐人街怎么走？离这儿远吗？
turns.pinyin: Mǎkè! tàihǎole! qǐngwèn, Tángrénjiē zěnme zǒu? lí zhèr yuǎn ma?
turns.en: Mark! Wonderful! Excuse me, how do we get to Chinatown? Is it far from here?

turns.name: 马克
turns.hanzi: 不远，很近。您往前一直走，到第二个路口往左拐。
turns.pinyin: bù yuǎn, hěn jìn. nín wǎng qián yīzhí zǒu, dào dì èr gè lùkǒu wǎng zuǒ guǎi.
turns.en: No, it's very close. Go straight ahead, and turn left at the second crossing.

turns.name: 陈爸爸
turns.hanzi: 左拐？然后呢？
turns.pinyin: zuǒ guǎi? ránhòu ne?
turns.en: Left? And then?

turns.name: 马克
turns.hanzi: 然后再往前走一百米，就到了。
turns.pinyin: ránhòu zài wǎng qián zǒu yī bǎi mǐ, jiù dào le.
turns.en: Then walk on another hundred metres, and you're there.

turns.name: 陈妈妈
turns.hanzi: 小伙子，你的中文真好！谢谢你！
turns.pinyin: xiǎohuǒzi, nǐ de zhōngwén zhēn hǎo! xièxie nǐ!
turns.en: Young man, your Chinese is so good! Thank you!

turns.name: 陈爸爸
turns.hanzi: 我们在伦敦住了很多年，还不认识路！
turns.pinyin: wǒmen zài lúndūn zhù le hěnduō nián, hái bù rènshi lù!
turns.en: All these years in London, and we still don't know the way!

turns.name: 陈妈妈
turns.hanzi: 晚上来饭馆吃饺子吧！
turns.pinyin: wǎnshang lái fànguǎn chī jiǎozi ba!
turns.en: Come to the restaurant for dumplings tonight!

turns.name: 马克
turns.hanzi: 好！不客气，晚上见！
turns.pinyin: hǎo! bùkèqi, wǎnshang jiàn!
turns.en: Great! You're welcome. See you tonight!

dialogues.title: The supermarket's next to the bank

turns.name: 陈妈妈
turns.hanzi: 小伙子！我们又见面了！
turns.pinyin: xiǎohuǒzi! wǒmen yòu jiànmiàn le!
turns.en: Young man! We meet again!

turns.name: 马克
turns.hanzi: 阿姨好！叔叔好！陈明，你好！
turns.pinyin: āyí hǎo! shūshu hǎo! Chénmíng, nǐhǎo!
turns.en: Hello, Auntie! Hello, Uncle! Hi, Chen Ming!

turns.name: 陈明
turns.hanzi: 欢迎欢迎！请坐！
turns.pinyin: huānyíng huānyíng! qǐng zuò!
turns.en: Welcome, welcome! Have a seat!

turns.name: 马克
turns.hanzi: 老板，请问，附近有没有超市？我想买水果。
turns.pinyin: lǎobǎn, qǐngwèn, fùjìn yǒu méiyǒu chāoshì? wǒ xiǎng mǎi shuǐguǒ.
turns.en: Excuse me, boss, is there a supermarket near here? I'd like to buy some fruit.

turns.name: 陈明
turns.hanzi: 有。出门往右走，超市在银行旁边。
turns.pinyin: yǒu. chūmén wǎng yòu zǒu, chāoshì zài yínháng pángbiān.
turns.en: Yes. Turn right out of the door, and the supermarket's next to the bank.

turns.name: 陈爸爸
turns.hanzi: 明天我们想带朵朵去大英博物馆。离这儿远吗？
turns.pinyin: míngtiān wǒmen xiǎng dài Duǒduo qù Dàyīngbówùguǎn. lí zhèr yuǎn ma?
turns.en: Tomorrow we'd like to take Duoduo to the British Museum. Is it far from here?

turns.name: 陈明
turns.hanzi: 不太远，走路十五分钟左右。坐公交车也很方便，车站就在饭馆对面。
turns.pinyin: bù tài yuǎn, zǒulù shí wǔ fēnzhōng zuǒyòu. zuò gōngjiāochē yě hěn fāngbiàn, chēzhàn jiù zài fànguǎn duìmiàn.
turns.en: Not too far, about fifteen minutes' walk. The bus is easy too: the stop is right across from the restaurant.

turns.name: 马克
turns.hanzi: 明天我也有空，我和你们一起去吧！
turns.pinyin: míngtiān wǒ yě yǒukòng, wǒ hé nǐmen yīqǐ qù ba!
turns.en: I'm free tomorrow too. I'll come with you!

turns.name: 陈妈妈
turns.hanzi: 你们伦敦人真热情！
turns.pinyin: nǐmen lúndūn rén zhēn rèqíng!
turns.en: You Londoners are so friendly!

turns.name: 陈明
turns.hanzi: 妈妈，我们北京人也很热情啊！来，先吃饺子吧！
turns.pinyin: māma, wǒmen běijīng rén yě hěn rèqíng a! lái, xiān chī jiǎozi ba!
turns.en: Mum, we Beijingers are friendly too! Now, have some dumplings first!

turns.name: 马克
turns.hanzi: 陈明，你怎么了？哪儿不舒服？
turns.pinyin: Chénmíng, nǐ zěnmele? nǎr bù shūfu?
turns.en: Chen Ming, what's the matter? Are you not well?

turns.name: 陈明
turns.hanzi: 我头疼，嗓子也疼。
turns.pinyin: wǒ tóuténg, sǎngzi yě téng.
turns.en: I've got a headache, and a sore throat.

turns.name: 小雨
turns.hanzi: 你发烧了吗？
turns.pinyin: nǐ fāshāo le ma?
turns.en: Have you got a temperature?

turns.name: 陈明
turns.hanzi: 有点儿发烧，三十八度。
turns.pinyin: yǒudiǎnr fāshāo, sānshíbā dù.
turns.en: A bit of one. Thirty-eight.

turns.name: 小雨
turns.hanzi: 你感冒了！你应该去看医生。
turns.pinyin: nǐ gǎnmào le! nǐ yīnggāi qù kàn yīshēng.
turns.en: You've got a cold! You should see a doctor.

turns.name: 陈明
turns.hanzi: 没事儿，就是感冒。多喝热水就好了。
turns.pinyin: méishìr, jiù shì gǎnmào. duō hē rèshuǐ jiù hǎo le.
turns.en: It's nothing, just a cold. I'll drink lots of hot water and be fine.

turns.name: 马克
turns.hanzi: 那你应该在家休息，今天别工作了！
turns.pinyin: nà nǐ yīnggāi zài jiā xiūxi, jīntiān bié gōngzuò le!
turns.en: Then you should rest at home. Don't work today!

turns.name: 陈明
turns.hanzi: 不行，星期六饭馆很忙，我得工作。
turns.pinyin: bùxíng, xīngqī liù fànguǎn hěn máng, wǒ děi gōngzuò.
turns.en: I can't. Saturdays are busy. I have to work.

turns.name: 小雨
turns.hanzi: 饭馆还有两个厨师呢！你是老板，你得回家睡觉！
turns.pinyin: fànguǎn hái yǒu liǎng gè chúshī ne! nǐ shì lǎobǎn, nǐ děi huí jiā shuìjiào!
turns.en: There are two other chefs! You're the boss. You have to go home to bed!

turns.name: 马克
turns.hanzi: 对！你回家吧，我去给你买药和水果。
turns.pinyin: duì! nǐ huí jiā ba, wǒ qù gěi nǐ mǎi yào hé shuǐguǒ.
turns.en: Exactly! Go home, and I'll go and get you some medicine and fruit.

dialogues.title: Could you do it a bit cheaper?

turns.name: 马克
turns.hanzi: 阿姨，请问，这儿有感冒药吗？
turns.pinyin: āyí, qǐngwèn, zhèr yǒu gǎnmào yào ma?
turns.en: Auntie, do they have any cold medicine here?

turns.name: 陈妈妈
turns.hanzi: 有。这个很好，你试试。你感冒了？
turns.pinyin: yǒu. zhège hěn hǎo, nǐ shì shi. nǐ gǎnmào le?
turns.en: Yes. This one's good, give it a try. Have you got a cold?

turns.name: 马克
turns.hanzi: 不是我，是陈明。多少钱一盒？
turns.pinyin: bù shì wǒ, shì Chénmíng. duōshǎoqián yī hé?
turns.en: Not me, Chen Ming. How much is a box?

turns.name: 陈妈妈
turns.hanzi: 六块五。陈明感冒了？他就是太累了！
turns.pinyin: liù kuài wǔ. Chénmíng gǎnmào le? tā jiù shì tài lèi le!
turns.en: Six fifty. Chen Ming's got a cold? He's just worn out!

turns.name: 马克
turns.hanzi: 苹果怎么卖？
turns.pinyin: píngguǒ zěnme mài?
turns.en: How much are the apples?

turns.name: 陈妈妈
turns.hanzi: 苹果四块一盒，橙子一块一个。
turns.pinyin: píngguǒ sì kuài yī hé, chéngzi yī kuài yī gè.
turns.en: Apples are four pounds a box, oranges a pound each.

turns.name: 马克
turns.hanzi: 有点儿贵。能便宜一点儿吗？
turns.pinyin: yǒudiǎnr guì. néng piányi yīdiǎnr ma?
turns.en: That's a bit expensive. Could you do it a bit cheaper?

turns.name: 陈妈妈
turns.hanzi: 我不是老板！你看，买两盒苹果，七块。
turns.pinyin: wǒ bù shì lǎobǎn! nǐ kàn, mǎi liǎng hé píngguǒ, qī kuài.
turns.en: I'm not the owner! But look: two boxes of apples for seven.

turns.name: 马克
turns.hanzi: 好，两盒苹果，一盒感冒药。一共多少钱？
turns.pinyin: hǎo, liǎng hé píngguǒ, yī hé gǎnmào yào. yīgòng duōshǎoqián?
turns.en: OK, two boxes of apples and a box of cold medicine. How much is that altogether?

turns.name: 陈妈妈
turns.hanzi: 一共十三块五。走，我们去看他。他得多喝热水！
turns.pinyin: yīgòng shí sān kuài wǔ. zǒu, wǒmen qù kàn tā. tā děi duō hē rèshuǐ!
turns.en: Thirteen fifty altogether. Come on, let's go and see him. He has to drink lots of hot water!

turns.name: 陈妈妈
turns.hanzi: 晚上好！几位？
turns.pinyin: wǎnshang hǎo! jǐ wèi?
turns.en: Good evening! How many of you?

turns.name: 陈爸爸
turns.hanzi: 三位。
turns.pinyin: sān wèi.
turns.en: Three.

turns.name: 陈妈妈
turns.hanzi: 这边请。这是菜单，你们先看看。
turns.pinyin: zhèbian qǐng. zhè shì càidān, nǐmen xiān kàn kan.
turns.en: This way, please. Here's the menu, have a look.

turns.name: 小雨
turns.hanzi: 服务员，点菜！来一个水煮鱼，一个宫保鸡丁。
turns.pinyin: fúwùyuán, diǎncài! lái yī gè shuǐzhǔyú, yī gè gōngbǎojīdīng.
turns.en: Waitress, we're ready to order! One boiled fish in chilli oil and one kung pao chicken, please.

turns.name: 陈妈妈
turns.hanzi: 水煮鱼要微辣、中辣还是特辣？
turns.pinyin: shuǐzhǔyú yào wēilà, zhōnglà háishi tèlà?
turns.en: Would you like the fish mild, medium or extra hot?

turns.name: 小雨
turns.hanzi: 特辣！
turns.pinyin: tèlà!
turns.en: Extra hot!

turns.name: 马克
turns.hanzi: 啊？小雨，我不能吃辣！
turns.pinyin: a? Xiǎoyǔ, wǒ bù néng chī là!
turns.en: What? Xiaoyu, I can't eat spicy food!

turns.name: 小雨
turns.hanzi: 好吧，那就微辣。马克，你也点一个菜吧。
turns.pinyin: hǎo ba, nà jiù wēilà. Mǎkè, nǐ yě diǎn yī gè cài ba.
turns.en: All right, mild then. Mark, you choose a dish too.

turns.name: 马克
turns.hanzi: 有没有不辣的菜？
turns.pinyin: yǒu méiyǒu bù là de cài?
turns.en: Is there anything that isn't spicy?

turns.name: 陈妈妈
turns.hanzi: 西红柿炒鸡蛋，一点儿也不辣。
turns.pinyin: xīhóngshì chǎo jīdàn, yīdiǎnr yěbù là.
turns.en: Tomato and egg stir-fry. It's not spicy at all.

turns.name: 马克
turns.hanzi: 好，来一份西红柿炒鸡蛋。别放辣椒！
turns.pinyin: hǎo, lái yī fèn xīhóngshì chǎo jīdàn. bié fàng làjiāo!
turns.en: OK, one tomato and egg, please. No chilli!

turns.name: 陈爸爸
turns.hanzi: 哈哈，这个菜没有辣椒！再来三碗米饭，一壶茶。
turns.pinyin: hāhā, zhège cài méiyǒu làjiāo! zài lái sān wǎn mǐfàn, yī hú chá.
